headline: Clean Tech Juggernaut Accelerates Past Auto Inc
text: Sales of electric, hybrid and CNG-powered passenger vehicles grew at more than double the pace of the automobile industry average, and accounted for nearly a third of the market last fiscal year, underlining rising inclination towards cleaner mobility among Indian buyers. Nearly 1.34 million units of these vehicles were sold in the year ended March 31, a 31% increase compared with 1.02 million units in FY25, show data collated from the government’s Vahan portal and the Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers. Total passenger vehicle sales rose 13% in the fiscal year to about 4.67 million units. The growing shift towards cleaner mobility will provide respite to the government amid India’s high dependence on oil and gas imports and the difficulty in sourcing fossil fuels due to the West Asia crisis. The Modi administration has had to cut taxes to shield consumers from higher petrol and diesel prices amid the supply crunch. The hard economics of expensive fossil fuels, and growing awareness about deteriorating air quality in cities are nudging buyers toward alternatives that promise lower running costs and a lighter carbon footprint. The demand growth is also supported by expanding charging and CNG supply infrastructure. A flood of new models is also hitting the road. The shift to cleantech is expected to accelerate amid tightening emission regulations and the crisis in West Asia, senior industry executives told ET. 'First and foremost, economics itself is driving up sales of CNG, hybrid and electric vehicles,' said Ashim Sharma, senior partner at Nomura Research Institute, also citing improving infrastructure and launch of new models. Hybrids offer the best of both worlds to buyers who want to drive longer distances at lower operating cost without having to worry about range, he said. Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles managing director and chief executive Shailesh Chandra cited improving consumer confidence in electric vehicles and wider participation by manufacturers, with all major companies launching new products to cater to the demand growth. CNG-fuelled vehicle volumes in the industry grew 20% and EV volumes surpassed the 200,000-unit milestone last fiscal year, he said. Maruti Suzuki, which recently launched its first electric vehicle, is also seeing growing traction for alternative fuel options. 'Demand for CNG is robust,' Partho Banerjee, senior executive officer (marketing and sales) at the country’s largest carmaker, said last week. There is good acceptance among customers for electric vehicles too, with more models on offer in the mainstream market, he said. While consumer popularity is growing, carmakers have lined up multiple EV launches over the next three to four years, amid tightening emission rules. Electric cars, in fact, are poised to dominate the launch portfolio of automakers in the coming months. Tata Motors is scheduled to introduce the Sierra EV shortly. Also on the cards are three new models from Vietnamese electric carmaker VinFast, and an electric SUV each from Toyota Kirloskar Motor and Kia India. New EVs that hit the road recently include Maruti Suzuki e-Vitara, Mahindra XEV 9s and Tata Punch EV. Tata Motors, which offers CNG options in five of its vehicles, posted 24% growth in sales in the segment at 170,000 units last fiscal year. Sales of its electric vehicles rose 43% to 92,000 units in the same period, Chandra said. 'Industry momentum is expected to sustain, led by growth in SUVs, CNG and EV.'

headline: Status Quo on Interest Rates Likely
text: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is expected to hold interest rates and keep its policy stance unchanged when the monetary policy is announced on Wednesday, according to 15 institutions surveyed by ET, as policymakers grapple with a sharply altered global backdrop amid the US-Israel conflict with Iran that has pushed up energy prices and raised fresh concerns over the fiscal deficit. The six-member monetary policy committee meets April 6-8 for the first time since the war broke out on February 28. While a policy pause is widely anticipated, economists said the RBI’s communication, particularly on the rupee and bond yields, will be closely scrutinised. Several respondents also expect the central bank to consider additional steps to shore up the currency amid persistent capital outflows. 'Further policy changes by the RBI and the India government to manage INR weakness could be likely,' said Michael Wan, senior currency analyst at MUFG Bank. 'These could include restrictions and higher import duties on gold and non-essential imports and a dedicated facility or FX swap window by the RBI so that oil marketing companies can tap dollars instead of going to the market.' Most economists expect the central bank will avoid an aggressive response for now, preferring to assess the impact of the war and higher oil prices on the economy. 'After two back-to-back circulars on the rupee, people are reminded of the 2013 playbook, but I think the story ends there,' said Abhishek Upadhyay, senior economist at ICICI Securities Primary Dealership. 'It’s not 2013 and we don’t have a situation of a run on the currency.' Highlighting risks without committing to a policy trajectory is a good template to follow, said Sakshi Gupta, principal economist at HDFC Bank. 'If there is a hawkish commentary, it is likely to be balanced by stating that inflation is expected to remain within the comfort zone,' she said. Gaurav Kapur, chief economist at IndusInd Bank, expects that the governor is likely to acknowledge rising risks to inflation, growth and the exchange rate, while highlighting macroeconomic and financial stability backed by adequate external buffers to absorb supply shocks. Markets will focus on the RBI’s assumed crude oil price, which underpins its growth and inflation projections. India’s retail inflation stood at 3.21% in February. In the last policy announcement on February 6, the RBI projected inflation for the first two quarters of FY27 at 4% and 4.2%, while GDP growth was seen at 6.9% and 7%, respectively.

headline: SIR 3rd Phase for 23 States, 6 UTs Unlikely to Start in April
text: The third and final phase of the special intensive revision of electoral rolls is unlikely to begin in April and may be launched only after June, ET has learnt. Election Commission of India wrote to chief electoral officers of 23 states and six Union Territories on February 19 to ‘complete preparatory work at the earliest’, stating that SIR could ‘start from April’. However, it is learnt that 16th census exercise, which started on April 1, has come in the way. All-important booth level officers, crucial to SIR, are usually government teachers/employees and utilised extensively in the census exercise too. Census 2027’s ongoing first phase — house listing and housing census — was launched on April 1 and will continue until September 30 with the same pool of manpower. An overlap with the first stage of SIR, enumeration of each elector spread out over a month, will become challenging for enumerators. Also, SIR takes at least three months and, in reality, it has stretched out even further in the second phase. Phase-II saw several cases of complaints from BLOs on deadline pressures and workload. That apart, this phase has thrown up fresh challenges, making scheduling even more difficult. Phase-II got caught in litigation and political opposition, with several state governments moving court against ECI over various facets of SIR which often led to schedule changes. Then emerged an additional issue of ‘logical discrepancies’ in roll documentation in West Bengal. The issue landed in Supreme Court and is still simmering in prolonged and tense adjudications. Unlike Bihar’s SIR, where ECI refused any deadline extension, second phase has seen several extensions and varied timelines across 12 states/UTs.

headline: ‘Labelling People of Ladakh Anti-National A Self-Goal’
text: Prominent climate activist Sonam Wangchuk on Sunday said that India was respected for its nationalistic border population unlike China and Pakistan, and that calling people of Ladakh as ‘anti-national’ was a ‘self-goal’ that needed introspection. Wangchuk addressed a huge gathering at Gandhi Park in Kargil, where Kargil Democratic Alliance organised a welcome programme for him after his release from jail. The members of Apex Body Leh, KDA members, Lok Sabha MP from Ladakh and LAHDC members were present at the function. ‘India is respected for its nationalistic population or borders unlike Pakistan and China where they have a lot of differences. It is unfortunate that a narrative of anti-national was spread against Ladakh. It is a self-goal and needs introspection,’ he said. Wangchuk also referred to remarks of Ladakh DGP who in a presser in September referred to him as ‘anti-national who has connections with Pakistan’. ‘I was branded as anti-national and connected to Pakistan. It was sad and baffling. All allegations were rejected by court. Now it is the time for them to explain. If I was wrong, then I should be in jail or else they should sincerely apologise,’ he said. Wangchuk said dialogue with the Centre should happen in a conducive atmosphere and people of Ladakh should remain united to press for their democratic and constitutional rights.

headline: Kerala Capital Fights Triangularly Poised
text: Assembly elections in Kerala’s capital city are being followed in the immediate context of BJP, for the first time, winning the mantle to rule the Thiruvananthapuram corporation less than six months ago by ending the CPI(M)-led LDF rule and pushing the Congress-led UDF to third position. If that makes these polls an occasion for BJP to try and expand its show to the city’s assembly segments, and for LDF and UDF a test on their capacity to fight back, then Vattiyoorkavu and Kazhakootam seats present a classic case of fierce triangular fight involving three principal rivals. In 2021, Left won these two seats after a fierce fight with BJP coming second, pushing Congress to third slot. The star line-up at Vattiyoorkavu includes young CPM MLA VK Prasanth, Congress heavyweight K Muraleedharan and BJP corporator R Sreelekha. A local resident said Prasanth is a young, energetic and accessible MLA, while Muraleedharan will have to convince voters he will not be moved out mid-term to fight other Congress electoral battles and Sreelekha faces questions over local BJP backing. BJP’s lead in Vattiyoorkavu in the last Lok Sabha and corporation polls and Left and UDF’s past victories make the fight a close suspense. In neighbouring Kazhakootam, the man at the centre of the Left’s hope, and the target of BJP and Congress, is CPI(M) MLA Kadakampalli Surendran, who was embroiled, as former minister for Devaswom, in the murky Sabarimala gold heist case. Despite the controversies, the Left is again betting on him since he is CPI(M)’s most entrenched local leader, with a knack to rally the election machinery. Senior BJP leader V Muraleedharan has positioned himself as the main challenger here, given a BJP candidate was second in the assembly seat last time. Many locals feel the votes of Congress candidate T Sarathchandra Prasad, a locally entrenched player, will have a bearing in tilting the balance.

headline: CM Vijayan Vows More Welfare, Development
text: A crowd, mostly women, gathered at Kulam Bazaar in Dharmadam, a coastal constituency about 15 km from Kannur town in Kerala, to hear chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan. The 80-year-old CPI(M) leader reached his constituency amid a whirlwind campaign. Vijayan focused his campaign on a surfeit of what he gave people: welfare schemes including pensions for low-income families and development programmes. ‘Public had a thought that development was not possible, we brought it, and I guess people want that to continue,’ Vijayan told the crowd. He also criticised the opposition, saying the United Democratic Front doesn’t ensure accountability for the state and the welfare of the people. Locals who have historically supported the Left expressed mixed feelings about the upcoming state government. They were, however, confident Vijayan would retain his seat. Some said the Sabarimala gold theft issue has affected public sentiment and the UDF might form the government this time, but Vijayan would still win here. Others said the chief minister interacts very little with people directly, though many residents highlighted his work in education and infrastructure and described Dharmadam as a ‘sure seat’. Dharmadam was declared Kerala’s first constituency free of extreme poverty in April 2025.

headline: Stalin Accuses EPS of ‘Lies, Deception’
text: Tamil Nadu CM MK Stalin on Sunday launched a scathing attack on Opposition leader Edappadi K Palaniswami, accusing him of building a campaign on slander, substandard rhetoric and misinformation. ‘If you say Palaniswami, it means lies and deception,’ he alleged at a rally in Virudhunagar. ‘He is hiding his own lies and telling lies repeatedly. The lies told by Palaniswami could be published as books; he is lying to that extent.’ He said everyone in the state was aware that despite the Union government collecting taxes to ‘benefit northern states’ and creating an ‘artificial financial crisis’ for Tamil Nadu, the DMK government had overcome those hurdles. ‘We have successfully implemented all our promises, including the pension scheme,’ he said. ‘Rather than holding the BJP-led Union government accountable, Palaniswami has chosen to target me. This is hardly surprising, considering he betrayed Jayalalithaa’s legacy by aligning with the very party she vehemently opposed.’ Stalin also defended the government’s coupon scheme, saying distribution of coupons instead of cash made allegations of commission-taking illogical.

headline: Muted Easter in Eateries of Poll-bound Puducherry
text: Restaurants in election-bound Puducherry were scrambling to find ways to offer a special brunch for customers on Easter owing to LPG shortage. The quaint White Town in the heart of the Union Territory is dotted with cafes that have traditionally served an Easter brunch to cater to the large Christian population and tourists. But this year, traditional menus were revisited and some brunches were shelved. Cafe Veloute owner John Peter said some signature dishes have been skipped because slow cooking was not feasible due to the LPG issue. Some restaurants scrapped their brunches entirely. Rendezvous owner Valerie Mathias said this was the first time in 32 years that there was no Easter brunch at the restaurant. ‘LPG cylinder prices in the black market have touched `5,000 and that is not feasible. We are considering if it is worth keeping the restaurant running or taking a break during the summer,’ she said. Bread & Chocolate said it was making bread and pizza in a woodfire oven, while a roadside eatery owner purchased a `20,000 firewood stove to tide over the period. Restaurateurs also raised concerns over restrictions imposed by authorities due to roadshows and rallies by prominent politicians. ‘The LPG issue coupled with polls happening at this time have kept tourists away and hit our business,’ Mathias said.

headline: Stalin, Welfarism Anchor DMK, says Kanimozhi
text: DMK’s parliamentary party leader Kanimozhi K said the party enters the election on the strength of its delivery. She said the governance record reflects improvements in human development indicators and steady economic growth, with Tamil Nadu among the better-performing states. Flagship welfare measures like the breakfast scheme and Magalir Urimai Thogai scheme have had a measurable social impact, while under chief minister MK Stalin the party has asserted the state’s rights within the federal system. Kanimozhi defended direct cash support, saying putting money in people’s hands boosts consumption, supports businesses and drives the economy. Schemes like the proposed Illathu Arasi initiative offering `8,000 coupons for household appliances are designed to combine empowerment with demand generation, she said. She described Vijay’s political impact as premature to assess and said the electorate makes informed choices based on governance, ideology and track record. On delimitation, she said Tamil Nadu has maintained that states which successfully implemented population control should not be penalised with reduced representation, and argued that delimitation should be based on the 1971 census rather than the 2011 census.

headline: Modi Flags Govt Failure in West Bengal; Mamata Urges Voters to ‘Stay Vigilant’
text: West Bengal CM Mamata Banerjee on Sunday called on women to ‘remain ready with broomsticks’ to resist any untoward incidents during the upcoming assembly polls, and warned that they must stay alert as the CAPF may conduct body frisking. ‘I have heard that women will be frisked thoroughly by CAPF. If anyone stops you from casting your vote, make sure to use your broom to clean the road. Our brothers will support you by standing behind you,’ she said. Banerjee referred to Bhabanipur candidate Suvendu Adhikari’s nomination rally and alleged that outsiders were present throughout the roadshow. ‘They ran amok, tearing down my posters and banners, spitting on our campaign material, harassing and heckling women bystanders, and even showing shoes at the sacred Maa Kali temple,’ she claimed. The Election Commission of India had directed the state chief secretary to suspend four police officials, including a deputy commissioner, for law and order failure during the roadshow and nomination in the Bhabanipur constituency and ordered disciplinary action against them. Banerjee also urged people whose names had been wrongly deleted from electoral rolls to immediately approach appellate tribunals, as applications had to be filed by April 6.

headline: ‘Jungle Raj’: PM Slams TMC over Malda Hostage Case
text: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday said the entire country was shocked by the recent incident in West Bengal’s Malda district, where seven judicial officers were held hostage by Trinamool ‘hooligans’, forcing the Supreme Court to intervene. The PM also asserted that he has full faith in ECI and that the polls will be conducted in an ‘impartial, intimidation-free manner’. ‘Just a few days ago, you saw how in Malda, judicial officers were held hostage. What kind of government and system is this, where the constitutional system itself is not safe? This is not just an example of Trinamool, but of the present state government’s maha jungle raj,’ Modi said while addressing a rally in Cooch Behar. He urged people to vote for ‘parivartan’, exercise their rights and bring about change. On polling day, he told the crowd, ‘No matter how much Trinamool goons try to intimidate you, have faith in law and order. In this election, fear will disappear and good governance and trust will be established.’

headline: Amid Welfare Push, Bidi Work Sustains Women in Malda Villages
text: Amid talks of women empowerment and other benefits of the Lakshmir Bhandar scheme touted by the Trinamool Congress, ET found that even in the remotest villages of West Bengal’s Malda district, women are self-employed and not solely dependent on the welfare scheme. In most houses visited in Malda’s remote parts, women roll bidis at home and have been doing it for years. One resident said bidi-making is a form of livelihood for her, while the household work and hearing-centre visits for SIR documents had made them lose money every day. Bidi-makers earn between `150 and `200 for 1,000 bidis rolled. The leaves are either procured from factories in a centralised place or from some households that collect and prepare them. In Sujapur, where name deletion in the special intensive revision of electoral rolls had people worried, the women who gathered to speak were also engaged in bidi-making. They said standing in hearing queues for hours had affected their earnings even as they continued to bind bidis every day.

headline: Siddu says PM’s Comments Timed at Polls in TN, Kerala
text: Chief minister Siddaramaiah on Sunday termed Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s recent assurance that southern states would not lose out in the proposed delimitation exercise as politically timed messaging ahead of upcoming assembly elections in Tamil Nadu and Kerala. He said he welcomed the Prime Minister breaking his silence on the subject, but questioned the timing and intent. Siddaramaiah stressed that the debate was not about whether the number of Lok Sabha seats would increase, but about the manner and distribution of that increase. He argued that the proposed expansion disproportionately benefits BJP-ruled or BJP-dominated states. Citing projections, Siddaramaiah said states such as Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Gujarat were likely to see significantly higher increases in parliamentary seats compared to southern states. Even if Lok Sabha expands to 816 seats, the southern states’ share remains around 24%, he said, adding that states which had performed better on population control and governance risked being disadvantaged. He called for wider consultations and public debate before undertaking structural changes to parliamentary representation.

headline: Assam CM’s Wife Holds Multiple Passports: Cong
text: The Congress on Sunday levelled serious allegations against Assam CM Himanta Biswa Sarma and his wife, Riniki Bhuyan Sarma. Addressing a press conference in New Delhi, Congress leader Pawan Khera claimed that documents received by the party from overseas sources indicated that the chief minister’s wife possessed three ‘active’ foreign passports, purportedly issued by the United Arab Emirates, Antigua and Barbuda, and Egypt. He questioned how an Indian citizen could allegedly hold multiple foreign passports, stating that Indian law does not permit dual citizenship. The party also alleged that overseas assets had not been disclosed in election affidavits.

headline: Rahul Attacks Sarma, Calls Him ‘Most Corrupt CM’
text: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Sunday attacked Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma, accusing him of corruption and divisive politics. Addressing a public rally in Biswanath, Gandhi alleged that Sarma is ‘the most corrupt CM in the country’ and that ‘Assam’s chief minister spreads hatred’. He said the people of Assam would one day demand accountability. Gandhi said the state belongs to figures such as Mahapurush Srimanta Sankardeva, Bharat Ratna Bhupen Hazarika, Gopinath Bordoloi, Azan Fakir, former CM Tarun Gogoi and singer Zubeen Garg. He added that Zubeen devoted his life to uniting Assam and never spread hatred. Gandhi further alleged that the state is being run for the benefit of a few corporates, with land being taken from locals and handed over to business groups. He promised Rs 450 as daily wages to tea workers and Scheduled Tribe status to six communities, saying earlier promises by the current government were never fulfilled.

headline: Pooled Natgas of 7mmscmd Flows to Priority Sectors
text: As the Iran war triggered a supply crunch, the government plans to supply about 7 million metric standard cubic meters per day of natural gas to city gas distributors, fertiliser makers and other users via a pooling mechanism. The supplies will be at around $11.60 per metric million British thermal unit, people familiar with the matter said. Last month, after Iran’s attack on Qatar’s LNG facility and the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz slashed India’s natural gas imports by about 60%, the government issued an order to regulate supplies. It drew up a priority ladder of gas-consuming sectors and tasked state-run Gail with overseeing the diversion of gas from non-priority to priority users. All diverted volumes were to be pooled and priced uniformly by the oil ministry. After consultations with producers and consumers and an assessment of available supplies and costs, a pool of about 7 mmscmd has been formed. Imports account for roughly half the volumes, with the rest largely sourced from Vedanta and deep-water output by Reliance Industries and ONGC. Gail, which will administer the supplies, is also expected to levy a charge of $0.20 per mmbtu on top of the gas price, a move consumers are pushing back against. About 2.5 mmscmd of the pooled volume is likely to go to city gas distributors, with the remainder allocated to fertiliser makers and other users.

headline: TPG to Buy NIIF Green Infra NBFC Aseem for `4000 cr
text: US buyout group TPG, along with consortium partners ICICI Bank and GIC of Singapore, has agreed to buy non-bank lender Aseem Infrastructure Finance Ltd for `4,000 crore as it looks to accelerate green funding and investment initiatives in the country, said people aware of the matter. The three sponsors of the NBFC will exit as part of this deal. A binding agreement will be finalised over the next few days. Aseem Infrastructure was set up six years ago to provide debt funding for long-term core sector projects with a special emphasis on clean energy. Its sponsors include the National Investment and Infrastructure Fund II, the government of India and Japan’s Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corp. The acquirers will take over the entire team, the `1,800 crore loan book as well as the Aseem brand. TPG had earmarked a $1 billion initial investment for a first-of-its-kind green financing platform in India under the aegis of TPG Rise Climate to help enterprises transition from legacy fossil fuel-based systems to greener options. Since then, it has roped in ICICI Bank and GIC of Singapore as co-investors for this yet-to-be-named platform.

headline: Platforms Brace for Impact as Gig Workforce Returns Home
text: Quick commerce, ecommerce and instant home service platforms are facing gig worker shortages as delivery riders and helpers return to their hometowns amid elections and the harvest season. According to industry executives, the daily active gig workers on quick commerce platforms are currently running 10-12% below early-2026 levels. The timing is particularly damaging. Typically, quick commerce as well as food delivery platforms see an uptick in demand during this period due to IPL matches. Order fulfilment for quick grocery delivery services in Delhi-NCR, Bengaluru and Mumbai is being delayed, a senior executive said, while slots on platforms like Snabbit, Urban Company and Pronto are going dark in several pockets. Platforms are offering higher incentives and ramping up hiring, but the supply-side squeeze is arriving ahead of schedule. Pronto founder Anjali Sardana said the segment expects some impact on supply due to the West Bengal elections, especially in northern cities where the company has some professionals from the state. Amid the workforce shortage in cities and macroeconomic uncertainties, demand for gig workers, especially delivery riders, could rise 25% in the coming months, according to hiring platforms.

headline: Semicon Mission 2.0 Set to Prioritise Memory Chips
text: India Semiconductor Mission 2.0 will prioritise advanced memory packaging focused on high bandwidth memory, officials told ET. ISM 1.0 was launched in 2021 as a push toward semiconductor manufacturing, packaging and design units. While the government has kept the public focus of the `1-lakh crore second phase on establishing the full semiconductor ecosystem, officials said potential investment applications for high bandwidth memory production will be given precedence. Critical for running artificial intelligence data centres, HBM prices have soared due to a multi-year global demand supercycle. Officials said there are also concerns over increasing technology controls by major economies and sudden economic shocks that may impact industry timelines. They said it is evident that HBM technology is crucial for the AI ecosystem and India intends to enter the manufacturing value chain. But manufacturing remains concentrated among a few players globally, with SK Hynix, Samsung and Micron dominating the market. Micron’s $2.5-billion plant in Gujarat’s Sanand, inaugurated last month, converts imported advanced DRAM and NAND wafers into finished memory chips and SSDs, but is not planned to host HBM manufacturing yet.

headline: Five Things About ‘Maven’, AI at the Heart of US War Machine
text: Project Maven is the Pentagon’s flagship artificial intelligence programme, launched in 2017 as a narrow experiment to help military analysts make sense of the torrent of drone footage pouring in from conflict zones. It has since evolved into an AI-assisted targeting and battlefield management system that accelerates the kill chain from detection to destruction. Maven functions like both the air traffic control of battle and its cockpit, rapidly fusing sensor data, troop intelligence, satellite imagery and force deployment information to determine the best course of action for striking a target. The emergence of ChatGPT broadened use of the technology, allowing more natural-language interaction with the system. Google was Maven’s original AI contractor, but withdrew after employee protests in 2018. In 2024, Palantir stepped into the space Google vacated and is now Maven’s primary technology contractor. US strikes have been carried out at a sustained pace, and Maven’s ability to speed up the targeting and firing process is seen as central. A recent Pentagon demonstration described how Maven turns an observed threat into a targeting workflow and presents commanders with options.

headline: Indian IT Cos Likely to Dodge West Asia War Volleys in Q4
text: While the impact of the ongoing West Asia war has been limited for Indian IT service companies so far, analysts in their fourth-quarter preview have highlighted some pockets of potential weakness for the industry. HDFC Institutional Research said the ongoing Middle East crisis poses a moderate short-term risk to Indian IT firms with exposure to regional energy and utility clients, as geopolitical uncertainty may delay discretionary spending and new projects while raising operational concerns regarding infrastructure resilience, travel and employee safety. Companies such as Tata Consultancy Services, Infosys, HCLTech, Wipro and Birlasoft derive 6-17% of their revenue from the energy and utilities sector, but the impact on existing projects is expected to remain contained because delivery operations are anchored offshore in India and mission-critical programmes typically persist despite regional volatility. Analysts across brokerages estimate a muted quarter for the IT services sector despite currency tailwinds. Tech Mahindra and L&T Technology Services face some direct impact from the regional situation, while other companies may see engagement delays and slower discretionary spending.

headline: Agentic Harness: Why AI Magic is in the Plumbing
text: Indian enterprises are betting big on AI agents, or software that autonomously books meetings, files reports and executes multi-step business workflows. Beneath the buzz lies the agentic harness, the software framework that wraps around an AI model and gives it the ability to act and not just respond. AI models can operate independently for simple one-step tasks, but they cannot function autonomously on complex, long-running or multi-step tasks. They cannot remember what happened the day before, send an email, or recover from a crash mid-task. The harness is the software layer that handles everything the model itself cannot. Open-source project OpenClaw functions as an agent harness, enabling large language models with scheduling capabilities, browser control, persistent memory and messaging channels. Anthropic’s Claude Code is another example, while Microsoft has built AutoGen for conversational multi-agent systems. In India, Hexaware launched Agentverse this year, but investors and analysts say there is still a gap in the ecosystem, with many thin wrappers calling themselves agentic.

headline: Record Run for Co, LLP Floats in FY26 Despite a Bump in March
text: India saw a record number of company and limited liability partnership registrations in FY26, though growth in the final month was the slowest amid uncertainty over the West Asia conflict, which dampened investor sentiment, a senior official said. Registration of companies rose to 247,658, up by 37% from 2024-25, while that of LLPs shot up by 40% to 95,965. This growth, however, tapered in March, with company incorporations showing only a 6% increase to 22,330, while LLP registrations were 9% higher at 9,489. Data showed that the number of foreign companies incorporated in India jumped to 96 in 2025-26 from 57 in the previous year. The war in West Asia has pushed up global energy prices and disrupted supply chains, posing risks to economic growth worldwide, including in India, a major energy importer. Officials said registrations may rise in 2026-27, albeit at a muted pace unless the conflict stretches beyond the June quarter and forces investors to pause their plans.

headline: Chouhan Takes Stock of Crop Losses from Heavy Rainfall
text: Agriculture minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan on Sunday took cognisance of heavy rainfall and hailstorm damage across several states, directing ministry officials to conduct a comprehensive review of crop losses and coordinate with state authorities to gather ground-level information. The minister is scheduled to hold discussions with the agriculture ministers of the affected states later in the day over the extent of crop damage. Chouhan assured farmers that the Modi government stood with them in this hour of crisis. The India Meteorological Department warned that a fresh Western Disturbance will affect Northwest India from April 7, triggering widespread rain, thunderstorms and hailstorms across Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Punjab, Haryana, Delhi and Uttar Pradesh through April 10. Hailstorms are forecast over several states, while heavy rainfall warnings remain in force in parts of the south and northeast. Agrometeorological advisories urged farmers to deploy hail nets, harvest matured crops without delay, drain excess water from fields and protect livestock and stored produce.

headline: Insolvency Cases: NeSL Enabling Real-time Access to Digital Debt, Claims Data
text: Information utility National E-Governance Services Ltd is enabling real-time access of digital records of default for adjudicating authorities to quickly retrieve debt and claims data of individuals and entities in insolvency cases. Records of default have evidentiary value in the process of insolvency resolution, NeSL managing director Debajyoti Ray Chaudhuri told ET. He said the latest amendments to the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code transform NeSL from a repository of financial information primarily accessed by financial creditors into a universal, legally mandated gateway for all insolvency proceedings. Under the recently approved IBC Amendment Bill, a record of default with the information utility and furnished alongside a financial institution’s application will be considered sufficient for the adjudicating authority to ascertain existence of default, removing ambiguity and eliminating the need for additional evidentiary material. Chaudhuri said the move will reinforce trust in the insolvency mechanism and facilitate faster authentication of records.

headline: Government Steps up Sale of 5-kg Cylinders
text: Sale of small 5-kg LPG cylinders, available across the counter at LPG distributorships on showing valid ID proofs, has been stepped up, with about 6.6 lakh bottles sold since March 23 as the government ramps up supplies to meet demand. Unlike the subsidised domestic 14.2-kg cylinders, the 5-kg bottles are priced at market rates and do not require any address proof for procurement from a nearby LPG distributorship. The oil ministry said more than 90,000 5-kg cylinders were sold on April 4 alone. It said there are no reports of shortages at LPG distributor points, with more than 51 lakh domestic cylinders delivered during the day and online bookings accounting for 95% of total demand. Authorities have intensified action against hoarding and black marketing, seizing over 50,000 cylinders since March and issuing more than 1,400 show-cause notices to LPG distributors, with 36 dealerships suspended.

headline: US Special Forces Rescue Downed Airman in Iran
text: US special forces rescued a downed airman in Iran in a complex operation that averted a potential crisis for President Donald Trump, who issued renewed threats to intensify attacks if Tehran did not reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Trump announced the rescue on social media, describing it as one of the most daring search and rescue operations in US history. The airman, the weapons officer of an F-15 jet shot down on Friday, was wounded but will be fine, Trump said. The pilot of the aircraft had been rescued on Friday. In another expletive-laden post, Trump repeated his demand that Iran open the Strait of Hormuz and warned of escalation. A US official said the rescue involved dozens of military aircraft and encountered fierce resistance from Iranian forces. The Wall Street Journal reported that two specially equipped aircraft used in the mission malfunctioned and were blown up by US forces. A senior administration official said the rescue had involved a CIA deception campaign inside Iran while the missing weapons officer was located in a mountain crevice and extracted.

headline: Iran Strikes Gulf Energy Infra, Hits UAE, Bahrain and Kuwait
text: Critical infrastructure across the Gulf came under attack from Iran on Sunday, with damage reported at civilian facilities in the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain and Kuwait. Gulf countries have faced repeated drone and missile attacks from Iran in recent weeks in response to US and Israeli strikes that began in late February. In Abu Dhabi, authorities said they were tackling fires at a petrochemical plant in Ruwais Industrial City on the UAE’s northwest coast. The emirate’s media office said the blaze at the Borouge facility was caused by falling debris following air defence interceptions. In Bahrain, the state energy company said a drone strike caused a fire at a storage tank, which was later extinguished without injuries. Kuwait’s electricity and water ministry said two power and desalination plants were damaged in a drone attack, forcing the shutdown of generating units and causing significant material damage. Iran’s army said it had targeted aluminium industries in the UAE and US military infrastructure in Kuwait.

headline: OPEC+ Moves to Raise Output as Iran War Chokes Oil Flows
text: OPEC+ agreed on Sunday to raise oil output quotas by 206,000 barrels per day for May, though the increase is largely symbolic as key producers remain constrained by the US-Israeli war with Iran. The conflict has effectively shut the Strait of Hormuz, the world’s most critical oil route, since late February, curbing exports from major Gulf producers including Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Kuwait and Iraq. Crude prices have surged to near four-year highs of around $120 a barrel, driving up fuel costs globally and prompting governments to act to conserve supplies. Analysts said the planned increase accounts for less than 2% of disrupted supply and is largely academic while Hormuz remains shut. Eight OPEC+ members agreed to the higher quotas at a virtual meeting, while Russia remains unable to raise output due to sanctions and war-related damage.

headline: Italy Airports Flag Jet Fuel Shortages as Iran War Bites
text: Several airports in Italy have issued advisories warning of limited jet fuel supplies in the coming days, as the Middle East conflict shows little sign of easing. Fuel restrictions have been introduced at airports including Bologna, Milan Linate, Treviso and Venice, according to notices to airmen. At Venice, priority is being given to medical, state and long-haul flights, while aircraft on routes under three hours may be limited to 2,000 litres of fuel. Similar measures apply at Bologna and Treviso. The notices cite limited availability of Jet A1 fuel from Air BP Italia. The curbs are among the first signs of fuel supply disruption in Europe affecting aviation operations after the conflict led to the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz, a key route for global crude, gas and jet fuel supplies.

headline: Ukraine Drone Strike Sparks Fire at Lukoil’s Norsi Refinery in Russia
text: A fire broke out at Lukoil PJSC’s Norsi refinery, one of Russia’s largest, after the latest Ukrainian drone strike on the country’s energy infrastructure. Falling drone debris damaged units at the refinery in the Nizhny Novgorod region, and the blaze was later contained, regional governor Gleb Nikitin said. The Novogorkovskaya thermal power plant and several residential buildings were also hit, though power supply was being restored. In the Leningrad region, air defences downed 19 drones, including near the Baltic port of Primorsk. Ukraine has stepped up strikes on Russia’s industrial and export infrastructure, targeting refineries, ports and fertiliser plants to curb revenues amid elevated global prices.

headline: Banks Pay Near 2-year High Rates on CDs Amid Tight Liquidity
text: Banks have raised funds through certificates of deposit at near two-year highs, reflecting intensified competition for resources and sustained pressure on liquidity with policy rates remaining steady. Data from the Clearing Corporation of India showed CSB Bank offered the highest rate at 8.32% for 91 days, while Ujjivan Small Finance Bank and Equitas Small Finance Bank raised funds at 8.25% for year-long maturities. HDFC Bank paid 7.6% for 33-day funds, far above what banks typically pay retail depositors for short-term deposits. Overall, HDFC Bank raised `23,090 crore during the last fortnight across tenors ranging from 33 to 327 days, Axis Bank raised `3,500 crore at 7.6% for 92 days, and IndusInd Bank raised `2,075 crore at around 7.5% for tenors ranging from 91 to 94 days. Bankers said the spike goes beyond normal year-end seasonality and reflects tight systemic liquidity, pressure linked to liquidity coverage ratio requirements and tactical balance-sheet management amid weak deposit mobilisation.

headline: Life After Insurance Healthcare Comes Home, So Do The Bills
text: An increasing share of healthcare is now being delivered beyond hospital walls. From post-surgery nursing and physiotherapy to chronic care, oxygen support, home dialysis and even ICU-level care at home, more families are opting for professional medical services in familiar surroundings. The shift is being driven by an ageing population, rising chronic illnesses, nuclear families, higher hospital costs and greater acceptance of home-based care after COVID-19. Home nursing, physiotherapy and oxygen support can be partly covered by health insurance after discharge, but only for a limited period. Services range from doctor visits, physiotherapy, nursing and caregiving to advanced care such as home dialysis and ICU set-ups at home. Costs vary sharply: physiotherapy sessions can cost upwards of `800, non-medical caregivers over `30,000-45,000 a month, skilled nursing care above `85,000 a month, chemotherapy at home `10,000-15,000 per session and peritoneal dialysis `2,000-2,500 a day excluding medicines and consumables. Standard health insurance policies usually cover post-hospitalisation expenses for 60 to 90 days, sometimes 180 days, if directly linked to the hospitalised condition and supported by bills. Beyond this window, long-term home care becomes an out-of-pocket burden, making a separate healthcare corpus crucial.

headline: Only 1 in 3 IPOs Brought Cheer in FY26
text: FY26 was a challenging year for the primary equity market, with most initial public offerings failing to earn returns since listing amid heightened volatility. Of the 109 mainboard IPOs listed in FY26, only 32, or about one in three, posted positive returns while just 16 yielded double-digit returns over the listing price. Among the top gainers were electric bikes maker Ather Energy, auto ancillary manufacturer Belrise Industries and Aditya Infotech. If offer price instead of listing price is considered, the proportion improves modestly, with 37 companies generating returns. Majority of the large IPOs based on issue size or money raised failed to generate returns, with only a quarter of the top 12 IPOs earning gains. Among the worst-performing IPOs were steel products maker VMS TMT, construction company Highway Infrastructure and renewable energy equipment provider Solarworld Energy Solutions.

headline: Can’t Step Forward, Cos Want Headroom
text: Amid longer voyages, uncertainties and delays in payments and cargo movements, banks want the Reserve Bank of India to clarify last week’s diktat to curb rupee weakness because it could backfire on genuine trades. Corporates have been banned by RBI from cancelling and rebooking forward contracts, a move aimed at stopping directional bets on the rupee. But companies facing war-induced disruptions fear the directive could restrict them from rolling over forward contracts if export payments are deferred or imported goods take longer to land. Bankers said the issue was discussed over the weekend and may be formally raised with RBI. They also want clarity on hedging of external commercial borrowings and on documentation for booking forwards against import-export flows. Some large corporates with overseas operations are said to be exploiting the wider gap between the offshore non-deliverable forward market and the onshore market by selling dollars offshore and buying dollars forward in India.

headline: Sadbhav Lenders Turn Down NARCL Offer, Settle it Out of Court
text: Lenders to Sadbhav Engineering have opted for out-of-court debt restructuring under the Reserve Bank of India framework, turning down a revised offer from National Asset Reconstruction Company. The decision follows a consortium-led resolution plan implemented on March 31 after receiving approval from lenders representing 77.83% by value and 60% by number. As part of the resolution, Sadbhav Engineering has finalised a `1,517 crore restructuring package. Fund-based loans will be restructured into convertible debentures, providing lenders with a staggered recovery mechanism, while a portion of the interest on these debentures and promoter debt will be converted into equity. NARCL had submitted a bid of about `470 crore for the account and later revised it down to around `371 crore, after which lenders chose restructuring over a sale to the bad bank, avoiding a lengthy insolvency process. Sadbhav had earlier been admitted to insolvency proceedings over defaults on operational dues, but the appellate tribunal later set aside the order after the company settled dues.

headline: Small Finance Banks Make it Big on Micro Revival
text: India’s small finance banks have ended FY26 on a strong note, recording higher-than-average business traction supported by the revival in microfinance lending. The five publicly listed differentiated banking entities that have shared business updates so far have shown over 20% growth in gross loan portfolios, significantly higher than the banking sector’s average credit expansion. AU Small Finance Bank reported a 21.3% year-on-year rise in assets under management to `1.40 lakh crore, Equitas’ AUM grew 21.6% to `46,183 crore, and Ujjivan logged 26.6% growth to `40,655 crore. Equitas and Ujjivan also reported growth in microfinance lending even as they focused on growing secured businesses to reduce concentration risk. Granular credit bureau data showed that till February, small finance banks’ cumulative microfinance portfolio had contracted from December levels, unlike other lender categories which had begun to see growth revival. Lenders’ collection efficiency has also improved, according to people aware of the development.

headline: CAIT Seeks Govt Action to Curb Malpractices of E-comm Cos
text: The government should take immediate and decisive action to curb the growing malpractices of certain e-commerce and quick commerce companies, as such activities are severely distorting India’s retail trade ecosystem, CAIT secretary general Praveen Khandelwal said on Sunday. He expressed serious concern over unchecked and unfair practices adopted by certain foreign-funded e-commerce entities, saying these are creating an uneven playing field for more than nine crore traders who form the backbone of the nation’s supply chain and employment ecosystem. He highlighted predatory pricing, deep discounting, dark patterns, inventory-led models disguised as marketplaces, preferential treatment to select sellers and the rapid expansion of dark stores as anti-competitive moves threatening the survival of small and medium traders. CAIT demanded early finalisation and implementation of a comprehensive National E-commerce Policy, along with stringent regulatory frameworks and robust enforcement mechanisms.

headline: Cancer Drug Cos See Side-effects of Platinum Surge
text: Manufacturing of cancer medicines such as carboplatin, oxaliplatin and cisplatin has become unviable due to a surge in the price of platinum, a critical component in these compounds, local drug producers claim. They have approached the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority seeking a 50% increase in the maximum price at which these products can be sold to patients. The ceiling price for carboplatin is `61.10 per 10 mg/ml vial, while for cisplatin it ranges from `70 to `300 depending on strength. Domestic companies such as Cipla, Intas, Dr Reddy’s Laboratories, Zydus Lifesciences, Emcure, Fresenius and Hetero are among the makers of these compounds. Industry executives said geopolitical uncertainty has pushed platinum prices to almost double in six months, in tandem with other precious metals, rising to over `8,000 per gram in February from `3,869 last September. They said the current ceiling price for carboplatin became commercially unviable in January itself. Platinum-based drugs form the backbone of treatment across multiple cancer types and are among the most affordable chemotherapy agents, but their low price point is now undermining manufacturing viability.

headline: Consumer Goods Cos Upbeat as GST Tailwinds Lift Volumes in March Qtr
text: Leading consumer goods makers and retailers, including AWL Agri Business, Dabur India, Marico, DMart and V-Mart Retail, reported a rebound in sales in the March quarter, driven by a recovery in volumes stemming from goods and services tax rationalisation in September. Companies remain optimistic about a further uptick in consumption in the coming quarters despite the Gulf conflict. Marico and Dabur India reported high single-digit year-on-year underlying volume growth in their domestic businesses, while staples player AWL Agri Business reported double-digit volume growth led by edible oils and industry essentials. Dairy major GCMMF, which owns the Amul brand, reported 11.4% growth in sales to `73,450 crore in FY26. On the retail side, V-Mart Retail reported 12% growth in same-store sales and a 24% jump in revenue, while Avenue Supermarts posted a 19% increase in sales. Companies said organised trade channels, including modern retail, ecommerce and quick commerce, sustained growth momentum during the quarter, alongside a gradual recovery in general trade. They said recent GST rate cuts and income tax relief for the middle class should support further consumption.

headline: Nykaa in Talks to Buy Majority Stake in Deepika Padukone’s Skincare Brand 82°E
text: Beauty and fashion retailer Nykaa is in negotiations with actress Deepika Padukone’s premium skincare brand 82°E to acquire a majority stake as it looks to bolster its House of Nykaa portfolio in an increasingly competitive market, said people aware of the development. Executives said the potential deal hinges on Nykaa’s market leadership, cumulative beauty customer base of 42 million and ability to build repeat orders and scale, helping turn around the flagging brand. 82°E is expected to continue holding a minority stake. The direct-to-consumer business, started by Padukone in late 2022 as a premium skincare label, saw revenue decline to `14.7 crore in FY25, down 30% from a year earlier, with a loss of `12.26 crore. Nykaa and Padukone already have an endorsement partnership, with Nykaa naming the actor its global brand ambassador last September. Analysts said celebrity brands often align with corporates for scale and profitability rather than building challenging standalone businesses.

headline: Wealthy Indians Turn to Alter Ego Trusts
text: Wealthy Indians, primarily those with assets spread across geographies or family members holding diverse citizenships, are increasingly turning to so-called alter ego trusts to manage succession planning and avoid lengthy court proceedings. Such structures help avoid complex, litigious situations during incapacity or after death, which may involve cross-border and religious considerations. The alter ego trust is settled for the benefit of the person who set it up and their spouse during their lifetimes, with the next generation named as remaindermen who get a defined portion of the inheritance. They differ from regular family trusts that require greater disclosure and can trigger disputes. Wealth advisers said interest is being driven by internationalised families, rising wealth and a desire for succession efficiency, privacy and risk mitigation. Assets settled into a trust during the settlor’s lifetime are governed by the trust deed, reducing scope for post-death disputes and ensuring continuity in management and distribution. Unlike probate proceedings, these structures also offer greater confidentiality.

headline: Audit Firms Wary as Govt Proposes to Tighten Rules
text: Audit firms in India have expressed concern about the proposed tightening of rules regarding auditor independence. They say the changes could disrupt audit economics, limit options for companies and lead to increased market concentration. The ministry of corporate affairs has proposed tighter auditor independence rules by amending the Companies Act to expand restrictions under Section 144. The proposed amendment would prohibit audit firms from providing non-audit services to clients for three years after stepping down. Industry experts said two elements stand out: the proposal bars ‘any’ non-audit services without clearly defining scope, and it extends the restriction for three years after the end of an audit tenure. BDO’s Yogesh Sharma said that while there is a concept of a cooling-off period before accepting an audit engagement in some overseas geographies, a cooling-off period for non-audit services after the end of an audit tenure is fairly unique. Firms argued that global networks already avoid even permitted non-audit work during the audit period, so extending restrictions further appears excessive and potentially anti-competitive.

headline: Classic Legends Plans to Grow Scrambler Portfolio
text: Premium motorcycle maker Classic Legends, owner of iconic brands Yezdi, Jawa and BSA, is embarking on a portfolio expansion with plans to introduce new bikes in the scrambler segment to carry forward its growth momentum. The company, which had broken into the top ten two-wheeler makers in the country by sales by volume in February, is seeking to consolidate its legacy in scrambler bikes built for off-road and street use. People aware of the development said it is preparing to introduce new motorcycles in the segment as part of its upcoming portfolio expansion. Co-founder Anupam Thareja said the company has seen strong rider response over the past year and will continue to strengthen its portfolio with authentic classic formats.

headline: Amul Turnover Rises 11% to over `1L crore
text: Dairy major Amul on Sunday said its total turnover rose 11% in the last fiscal year to cross the `1 lakh crore milestone on better demand for dairy products. The Gujarat Cooperative Milk Marketing Federation said the total unduplicated revenue of the Amul brand crossed the `1 lakh crore mark in FY26. It said the turnover of GCMMF, which owns the brand, grew 11.4% to `73,450 crore in the fiscal from `65,911 crore in the preceding year.

Why output hike by Opec+ won’t cool oil prices
text: With the Strait of Hormuz blocked, about 20% of energy supply from the Gulf nations has been nearly cut off for over a month. Supplies from Russia and Iran are flowing due to temporary waivers on the US sanctions. Global demand from these two sources, as well as alternative markets in Africa and South America, have surged. In a 12 March report, the International Energy Agency said that with supplies down from about 20 million barrels before the war to a trickle now and storage filling up, the Gulf countries have cut their oil output by at least 10 million barrels per day. It said global oil supply is seen plunging by 8 million bpd in March. The eight Opec+ countries—Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, UAE, Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria and Oman—on Sunday committed to back oil market stability and decided on a production adjustment of 206,000 bpd in May from the 1.65 million barrels of additional voluntary adjustment announced in April 2023. The grouping’s joint ministerial monitoring committee also highlighted the importance of safeguarding international maritime routes to ensure uninterrupted flow of energy. It expressed concern regarding the recent attacks on energy infrastructure, and said that restoring damaged energy assets to full capacity was both costly and time-intensive, thereby affecting global supply of the crucial fuels. Unlikely. At the time of writing this piece, the Brent June contract on ICE traded at $108.60 a barrel, up 0.3% from its previous close. Experts say the output hike may not ease prices due to prospects of a prolonged war and the Strait of Hormuz blockade. Alternative fuel sources also won’t be able to offset the 20% cut in supply from West Asia. Major consuming nations’ panic has also made suppliers such as Russia and Iran sell their oil at a premium or lower discounts. Reuters said that Ukraine’s attacks have hurt about 40% of Russia’s oil export capacity, which may tighten global supplies even more. The war-led market volatility has significantly hit India. Though crude oil, petrol and diesel supplies have been comfortable so far, retail prices of premium petrol and diesel and of industrial diesel have been hiked by state-run oil marketing firms. Private players Nayara and Shell have raised normal petrol and diesel prices too. Government says the country has secured crude supply for two months’ need. In a bid to avert price hikes in regular auto fuels, the Centre has slashed excise duty on them by ₹10 per litre, resulting in a gross fortnightly loss of about ₹7,000 crore to the exchequer. Last month, the IEA unanimously agreed to make 400 million barrels oil from their emergency reserves available to the market to address the supply disruptions. This is the largest ever release from reserves. This is the sixth time that the agency’s members have taken emergency action to support oil markets in the history of the IEA, which was created in 1974. Previous collective actions were taken in 1991, 2005, 2011, and twice in 2022.

headline: FAST-FOOD CHAINS BET ON INDIA BOOM
text: Subway—the ubiquitous sandwich shop—ranks among the largest US restaurant brands by store count. Yet its footprint in the world’s largest economy is shrinking. More than 600 outlets shut in 2024, and by December 2025 the US network fell below 20,000 for the first time in two decades. This decline reflects intensifying competition, shifting consumer preferences, over-aggressive expansion in earlier years, and changing location dynamics. The picture in India could not be more different. Subway opened its first outlet in a New Delhi mall in 2001. It reached 100 stores by 2010, 600 by 2017, and crossed 1,000 in 2026. Growth has been steady, in sharp contrast to the decline in the US market. Like other fast-food chains, Subway sits within India’s QSR industry, which is riding the country’s growth tailwinds. The industry is complex and varied, spanning small, independent, neighbourhood Udipi-style eateries to homegrown chains such as Haldiram’s and Saravanaa Bhavan, and global franchises like Subway and McDonald’s. Yet the organized segment is dominated by a handful of firms controlling global brands, with estimated revenues of about ₹20,000 crore in 2024-25. The top five companies are listed, and reports suggest that Subway may be eyeing an initial public offering. The segment has seen a surge in fundraising, mergers and acquisitions, and consolidation; all of which signal strong growth prospects. A Mordor Intelligence report estimates India’s QSR industry will grow at a compound annual growth rate of over 9% during 2026-31, to reach $47.3 billion in 2031. The outlook is underpinned by rising incomes, changing demographics, and the rise of food aggregators and delivery platforms. Rising incomes allow households to indulge in greater discretionary spending, including eating out. As incomes rise, there is a tendency to seek out a variety of cuisines and food choices, and a large part of that experience is derived from out-of-home food. Macro-level data supports this theory: between 2013-14 and 2023-24, aggregate private final consumption expenditure on restaurants and hotels grew at an 8.1% CAGR, almost double the 4.4% growth in food expenditure, and in line with the 11% growth in per capita GDP. Granular data also shows a shift away from home-cooked food, especially in the more affluent segments. Shifting demographics favour the QSR industry. Urbanization typically results in a breakdown of the traditional joint family structure, which is replaced by nuclear families or even single-person households. Shrinking urban households often have more than one earning member; busy lifestyles and long commutes result in a willingness to pay for services that are time-saving and convenient. Here’s where QSRs come in: a multi-income family can afford to order in or eat out more often than earlier generations. In fact, UPI transaction data reveals that fast food restaurants and other eating places are among the top merchant categories, and now account for a quarter of the total volume of spending. India’s demographic profile is also fuelling an eating-out culture. With 381 million Gen Z consumers and 339 million millennials, the country offers a vast QSR customer base. A wide mix of cuisines, coupled with strong localization, caters to diverse preferences. The growth of food aggregators and delivery platforms has reshaped the QSR industry—for better and worse. Delivery now accounts for 40-70% of QSR sales, depending on the brand and type of food ordered. The good news is that delivery platforms have boosted reach, especially of smaller outlets. At the same time, aggregator commissions have squeezed restaurant operating margins. As the consumption journey becomes more digital, QSRs will have to rework their business models to stay profitable.

headline: Govt eyes induction stove loan subsidy
text: India is planning a major push to increase the share of electric cooking stoves in its kitchens, as a shortage of cooking gas triggered by the West Asia war continues to hit households. The plan may involve bringing multilateral financial institutions to arrange zero-interest loans through state-run Energy Efficiency Services Ltd. The EESL is likely to redesign and ramp up the three-year-old National Efficient Cooking Programme to meet a surge in demand for what was largely a niche product before the conflict, two people aware of the matter said. Under the model under consideration, a third party would subsidize the interest on equated monthly instalments, lowering the cost burden for economically weaker consumers. The existing programme has no provision for an interest subsidy. “EESL is in talks with several financial institutions including World Bank and ADB,” one of the two people said. “It would be a sort of subsidy on the interest, which the financial institutions can support with.” Once the loan from the multilateral institution is tied up, EESL will use it to support zero interest loans for induction stoves. Under this model, a tie-up with financing private or public sector banks may be worked out wherein if a person procures a cookstove from EESL on EMI, then the consumer needs to pay only the principal part of it every month, and the interest will be paid by the financial institution. Demand for electric cookstoves shot up after the West Asia war began, as consumers rushed to compensate for a shortage in LPG cylinders. As demand rises, procurement of cooktops by EESL under the scheme is also being scaled up. A tender for 100,000 cookstoves has recently closed and two more tenders are scheduled for a total of 500,000 units. Given the demand, the phase-wise target may have to be revised. The programme was launched with a target of deploying 2 million cookstoves. Nearly 65% of India’s annual LPG demand of 33 million tonnes is imported—about 90% from West Asia—exposing households to global disruptions and putting pressure on the country’s import bill. Kirit Parikh said the shift towards induction-based cooking is needed urgently since most LPG is imported and the imports are concentrated. Saurabh Kumar said induction cookstoves can very well replace LPG, but availability and awareness will be key, and one way to ensure efficient adoption is to link the programme to PM Surya Ghar Yojana so households already using solar power can be approached easily.

headline: Crash, plane crunch drive traffic pain for airlines
text: India's domestic air passenger traffic growth was already cooling from the highs of post-pandemic revenge travel. Last fiscal is estimated to have been the worst since then because of multiple setbacks—grounded planes, frequent disruptions and heightened regulatory scrutiny after the country’s worst air crash in decades. Air passenger traffic rose 1.6% between April and February, according to Icra. The ratings agency estimates an up to 3% growth in fiscal year 2026. The number of Indians flying grew by 59% and 56% in FY22 and FY23, respectively. This growth slowed to 16% in FY24 and 7.6% in the following year. The slowdown, however, does not represent a lack of demand. Passenger load factor, a measure of occupancy levels in a flight, remained elevated at around 93%. The fatal Air India crash in June 2025 triggered heightened regulatory scrutiny and stricter safety checks across the industry. This led to lower aircraft utilization and operational delays. The operational meltdown in December at IndiGo led the DGCA to cut 10% of its daily flights. Another major drag has been aircraft availability. According to Icra, 13-15% of the industry’s fleet remained grounded as of February 2026, primarily due to engine failures and supply chain constraints. This directly reduced the number of planes in operation, limiting capacity addition even as demand remained robust. International passenger traffic has also taken a hit because of the closure of Pakistani airspace and restrictions in West Asia airspace due to the US-Iran war, forcing airlines to reroute long-haul flights. The war has also driven up fuel costs, resulting in higher fares and additional surcharges. Indian airlines carried 30.3 million international passengers in the first 10 months of FY26, a year-on-year increase of 8.5%, compared with stronger growth in FY25. Despite the slowdown, India’s top airlines are planning major expansion. By 2035, IndiGo plans to add 900 aircraft, Air India 541, and Akasa Air 189. Icra expects the aviation industry to report losses of ₹17,000-18,000 crore in FY26, with only some improvement in FY27, and has changed its outlook for the sector to negative from stable due to ongoing uncertainties. Some analysts still believe the FY27 outlook is stable, subject to geopolitical developments, and that industry growth is likely to remain in high single digits, driven more by aircraft supply than demand.

headline: Samsung to Xiaomi raise smartphone prices by up to 40%
text: The West Asia war and a memory chip scarcity have finally spilled over into smartphone prices, with leading smartphone makers raising prices by as much as 40%. India’s top three smartphone brands Vivo, Oppo and Samsung, and their smaller rivals Realme and Xiaomi, have raised prices across their portfolios, company emails to retailers show. The hikes are significant: smartphones make for India’s single-largest electronics category, with sales of over $43 billion through 2025. However, the segment has struggled since the covid pandemic in 2021, as the market got increasingly saturated. While companies so far managed single-digit revenue growth on the back of rising premium phone sales, the current market conditions come as a double whammy: consumers are deferring phone purchases due to rising prices of basic needs such as cooking gas even as the rise in prices does nothing to aid the ailing market. Vivo India increased prices of multiple phones over three tranches from October to March. Samsung increased prices across its mid-range smartphones, including the Galaxy A56 and A36 lines, which returned in slightly modified avatars at much higher prices. Oppo increased prices of five models by up to 18%. Vivo, Samsung and Oppo accounted for 47% of the 152 million smartphones sold in the country last year, according to IDC India. Taking Realme and Xiaomi into account, these five brands represent two-thirds of all smartphones sold in India every year. Analysts and retailers said the price increases are very likely just the start. According to Counterpoint India, memory chip prices for smartphones have gone up by over 120% from December to February. This has led to significant disruption, which was absorbed over the past three months due to available inventory with retailers. Now, the impact is being felt. The cost of a memory chip is up to almost 40% of a smartphone’s bill of materials cost from about 18% before. Component makers are increasing prices to meet demand, and with consumer demand stagnant, brands are now passing the cost on to their retail networks. Retailers said they have already been told the current price hikes are permanent and further increases are likely in coming quarters as memory chip prices are unlikely to reduce before the first half of 2027. Some price increases are also due to rising costs of commodities such as plastic used for moulding phones because of the West Asia war. The current price increases could lead to a drop of almost 10% in annual smartphone sales in India and a similar crash in net smartphone market revenue. Consumers are spending money only on necessary commodities as the cost of fuel and cooking gas rises, and smartphone upgrades are being delayed as buyers turn to the second-hand market or temporary repairs.

headline: Government eyes biodegradable sachets to tackle plastic litter surge
text: The government is working on an ambitious plan to encourage consumer goods makers to use biodegradable sachets to reduce plastic litter, curb soil pollution, and prevent drain blockages. The department of consumer affairs' plan involves transitioning a wide range of sachet-based products to eco-friendly packaging by developing plastic-free, biodegradable alternatives for one of the most widely used packaging formats in the country, two people aware of the matter said. The plan involves engaging all stakeholders and encouraging them to adopt it step by step, starting with a few products on a pilot basis. To start with, the ministry has planned to work towards replacing sachets used for pan masala and gutkha, which are a key contributor to littering in both urban and rural areas. While their low cost and convenience have made plastic sachets a staple, the small packs also represent one of the largest sources of plastic litter. This comes against the backdrop of India’s ban on single-use plastic. The country generates around 3.5 million tonnes of plastic waste annually, according to the Central Pollution Control Board, and around 40% is littered and remains uncollected. Sachets are used across many product categories including personal care items, pan masala, gutkha, instant coffee, spices, sauces, dairy whitener, detergent powder, dishwashing liquid and floor cleaners. Pan masala and gutkha are widely consumed across India and largely sold in small sachets. Designed for strength and shelf life, these sachets are among the highest-volume single-use packaging formats, with tens of billions produced annually. Manufacturers shifted to multi-layered paper-based laminates to comply, but these sachets remain non-biodegradable and difficult to collect or recycle due to their small size and mixed materials. Many end up as litter in streets, drains, fields and water bodies. The continued use of plastic-based adhesives, especially in the informal sector, further weakens the rules. This calls for biodegradable, plastic-free and scalable sachet alternatives for pan masala, gutkha and other consumer goods widely used in sachets. Industry executives said the transition is doable, but the key issue is the higher costs, as biodegradable sachets are more expensive than plastic ones.

headline: India raises gas supply for fertilizer companies
text: India has increased the allocation of natural gas to urea plants as supply improves after disruptions due to the Middle East crisis, according to the oil ministry. Overall gas supply to fertilizer plants has been raised to about 90% of their average consumption, from 70% to 75%, the ministry said. India had faced supply constraints after liquefied natural gas shortages linked to the Iran war forced some urea manufacturers to shut their plants ahead of the monsoon planting season. LNG is a key raw material to produce the crop nutrient, and the nation is the world’s largest importer of urea. The government made the decision to increase the gas allocation based on available inventory and scheduled LNG arrivals, and no dry-outs have been reported at LPG distributorships. India is also looking to secure imports, with Indian Potash issuing a tender to buy 2.5 million tonnes of urea ahead of the sowing season.

headline: BofA cuts Indian cos’ earnings estimates
text: Despite rising optimism, Amish Shah, head of India research at BofA Global Research, remains unconvinced by the India outperformance story, expecting the country to lag its emerging-market peers and cutting his earnings growth estimates for Indian companies for the second time in a row. He said crude prices have risen and some energy infrastructure assets in West Asia have been affected by the war. Even if tensions ease, supplies are unlikely to return to pre-war levels soon, keeping prices elevated for longer. This is expected to affect growth and keep commodity prices, including aluminium and copper, elevated. Brent crude oil prices have shot up by over 42% since the war broke out at the end of February. Given this, BofA saw little point in waiting for May earnings announcements and instead built in more realistic estimates to arrive at revised price targets. The brokerage has cut its 2026-27 Nifty earnings growth further to 8.5% year-on-year, down from 11% in early March and 14% pre-war. Since the war in West Asia began, the Nifty 50 and S&P BSE Sensex have slumped by around 9% each, while the Nifty Midcap 100 and Nifty Smallcap 250 have fallen as well. Shah said there is scope for a rally if the conflict ends, but a prolonged war remains the biggest risk factor for equities even now. He added that even if the conflict ends by the end of 2026, foreign flows are unlikely to turn meaningfully positive, though persistent outflows could ease with some reversal.

headline: ‘Global economy in permanent volatility’
text: Trade fragmentation, along with the ongoing West Asia conflict, means that 2026 could prove more challenging, as the global economy moves from episodic shocks to a state of permanent volatility, finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on Monday. However, India has sufficient fiscal space to sustain its asset-creating public expenditure, while the central bank has room to cut interest rates to support growth, aided by the government’s commitment to fiscal prudence, she said. The escalation of the Middle East conflict has evolved from a regional security concern into a systemic tremor, threatening the vital arteries of global energy and hardening the lines of a new multipolar world order, Sitharaman said at an event organized by the National Institute of Public Finance and Policy in New Delhi. The US and Israel launched coordinated strikes on Iran on 28 February, triggering retaliation and a wider regional conflict, with Tehran blocking access to the strategic Strait of Hormuz through which about a fifth of global oil trade passes. Sitharaman said 2025 was monumental in more ways than initially expected. Trade fragmentation has introduced severe uncertainty into global supply chains. This led to sharp downward revisions in global growth forecasts, but the year ended more optimistically than previously perceived, particularly for India. The finance minister also noted that global public debt has surged to approximately $106 trillion, exceeding 95% of global gross domestic product.

headline: India’s services sector slows as Iran war dents demand
text: India’s services sector grew at its slowest pace in 14 months during March, mirroring the slowdown in the growth of new business intakes, as the West Asia conflict hit domestic demand, a private survey showed. The HSBC India Services Purchasing Managers’ Index, compiled by S&P Global, fell to 57.5 in March from 58.1 in February, marking the weakest rate of expansion in 14 months but remaining above its long-run average of 54.4. Despite the slowdown in growth, the sector saw a record increase in international orders, while input cost pressures remained at their most intense since mid-2022. While new business gains continued to underpin growth, output was constrained by the detrimental impact of the West Asia war on demand, market conditions and tourism, the survey said. Intakes of new work rose at the slowest pace since January 2025. Softer increases in sales were noted in finance and insurance, real estate and business services, and transport, information and communication. Conversely, all four categories recorded quicker expansions in new export orders, causing overall growth in foreign sales to approach a series peak. Panelists noted gains from Africa, Asia, Australia, Europe, the Americas and the Middle East. HSBC said India’s services sector stayed in expansion mode in March, but growth momentum eased for a second consecutive month. Demand remained resilient, led by new export orders, yet input cost inflation accelerated to its fastest pace since 2022, indicating that higher fuel, transport and logistics costs are feeding into services. Of the four broad areas monitored, the quickest increases in input costs and output charges were seen in consumer services and finance and insurance, respectively. The latest report also showed a third consecutive monthly increase in employment. The pace of job creation was the strongest since mid-2025 as business confidence boosted hiring.
