Firms were at their most upbeat on the outlook for output in close to 12 years, underpinned by hopes of an improvement in demand and market conditions, as well as advertising and better customer relations. The HSBC India Composite PMI Output Index also fell from 58.9 in February to 57.0 in March, marking the weakest rate of expansion in nearly three-and-a-half years.

headline: Moody’s retains Baa3 rating for India but warns of risks from war
text: International rating agency Moody’s retained its Baa3 (BBB-) sovereign credit rating for India with a stable outlook, but warned that the ongoing conflict in West Asia would moderate real GDP growth to 6% in FY27 and raise inflation risks. The stable outlook incorporates India’s gradually improving fiscal metrics since emerging from the pandemic and resilient growth prospects compared with peers, the rating agency said.

headline: Summer crop sowing inches up; rice cultivation area declines
text: India’s summer crop sowing has edged up marginally so far this season, with higher acreage under pulses, coarse cereals and oilseeds offsetting a sharp decline in rice, amid concerns over input supplies following the war in West Asia. Total area under summer crops stood at 5.82 million hectares as of 3 April, up from 5.78 million hectares a year earlier, according to the ministry of agriculture.

headline: Cost of home-cooked veg thali flat in March, non-veg falls 1%: Crisil
text: The cost of a home-cooked vegetarian thali remained unchanged year-on-year in March, while the price of a non-vegetarian thali declined by about 1%, mainly because of lower broiler prices, according to the latest Crisil Roti Rice Rate report. The report calculates the average cost of preparing a thali, or a meal, based on prevailing input prices across north, south, east and west India.

headline: RBI rate-setting panel begins meet; decision on Wednesday
text: The Reserve Bank of India’s rate-setting panel on Monday started its three-day brainstorming session on the first bi-monthly monetary policy of the fiscal amid expectations of a status quo on the benchmark lending rate in view of apprehensions of a spike in inflation due to the West Asia war. The decision of the six-member Monetary Policy Committee will be announced on Wednesday.

headline: GeM facilitates transactions worth ₹5.03 trillion in 2025-26
text: Public procurement platform Government e-Marketplace facilitated transactions worth ₹5.03 trillion in 2025-26, down 7.4% from the previous fiscal, a senior official said. GeM facilitated transactions worth ₹5.43 trillion in 2024-25. GeM chief executive officer Mihir Kumar said the decline in growth can be attributed to a reduced contribution from the coal ministry, whose share in total sales fell from 34% to 20% in 2025-26.

headline: Central bank proposes tighter rules for bank agents
text: The Reserve Bank of India on Monday proposed tighter rules for bank agents delivering last-mile services in rural and underbanked regions, including stricter oversight, revised pay structures and stronger due diligence. The central bank outlined plans to reclassify and regulate business correspondents under two distinct models, enhance monitoring, and revise compensation structures.

headline: Serum Institute, Trivitron in talks to take MyLab global
text: Adar Poonawalla-led Serum Institute of India is in talks to partner with medical device maker Trivitron Healthcare to scale up its investment in MyLab Discovery Solutions and expand the Pune-based diagnostics provider’s operations internationally, according to people familiar with the matter. Chandra Ganjoo and Gurinder Bir Kaur have been listed as directors on the board of a new joint venture, Mylab Trivitron Next Gen Technologies, according to a legal filing. The deal is in advanced stages of due diligence and the final contours are yet to be decided. A separate entity has been created to get rid of MyLab’s debt and facilitate the investment. MyLab founder Hasmukh Rawal said the joint venture is being structured for better international opportunities in distribution and manufacturing with Trivitron’s global reach and presence, with a focus on high-end technologies. MyLab will benefit from Trivitron’s manufacturing capabilities to bolster its presence in in-vitro diagnostics and molecular diagnostics in India and overseas markets. Set up in 2016, MyLab develops and sells diagnostic kits used in human diagnostics, food safety, agriculture and veterinary medicine. The Poonawalla group holds 49% in the firm. MyLab’s income and operating margin fell after covid, with revenue dropping sharply before recovering to ₹147 crore in FY24 with a profit of ₹1.8 crore. Chennai-based Trivitron manufactures and trades medical equipment, devices and consumables, has joint ventures with global medical technology players and has a presence in Turkey, Finland, the US and China.

headline: E-bike firm Matter eyes $50 mn in fresh round
text: Electric motorcycle manufacturer Matter Motor Works is seeking to raise fresh capital in a Series C funding round. The company is in discussions with existing and new investors to support market expansion this financial year and the round could value the company at around $300 million post-money, according to people in the know. Co-founder Mohal Lalbhai confirmed the fundraise and said the company is raising around $50 million. The round is being led by existing investors including Capital 2B and JAL Innovation Fund, and is likely to close within three months. The fundraising comes as India’s electric motorcycle segment struggles to gain traction despite policy support and investor interest. Battery-powered motorbikes contributed less than 1% of the 1.14 million electric two-wheelers sold during FY25, according to Niti Aayog.

headline: InCred Alt secures ₹1,500 crore for its maiden credit fund
text: InCred Alternatives has closed its maiden special opportunities credit fund with a corpus of ₹1,500 crore, joining a growing wave of investment firms entering India’s expanding private credit market. The fund has raised capital from domestic family offices, ultra-high-net-worth individuals and international investors. About 75% of the fund has already been deployed across sectors such as auto, power, oil and gas, and hospitality. The fund primarily focuses on old-economy businesses with hard asset coverage, established cash flows and clear structural downside protection built in at the time of investment. InCred Group said its alternatives arm, launched in 2022, has built a track record in origination, underwriting, active portfolio management and income distribution.

headline: Wipro secures $1 billion contract from Singapore’s Olam Group
text: Wipro has bagged a $1 billion, eight-year contract from Singapore-headquartered food processing major Olam Group, marking its first mega deal in nearly six years. As part of a broader engagement, India’s fourth-largest IT services provider will acquire Mindsprint, Olam’s IT arm, for $375 million in an all-cash deal. The Bengaluru-based firm will manage Olam’s end-to-end IT transformation services. Olam committed to spend at least $800 million over eight years in modernizing its IT systems with an option to spend more than $1 billion in total. Wipro’s shares opened higher after the announcement. The acquisition gives Wipro access to Mindsprint’s agri-domain platforms and capabilities. The deal comes at a time when Wipro is staring at the possibility of a third straight year of revenue decline amid an uncertain macroeconomic environment due to the war in West Asia. Wipro’s management said the deal would expand its footprint in the food and agribusiness industry and scale the impact of Wipro Intelligence across the farm-to-fork value chain.

headline: Gulf funds agree to back Paramount’s $81 bn Warner takeover
text: Paramount has received signed equity commitments of close to $24 billion from three sovereign-wealth funds led by Saudi Arabia to help back its takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery, according to people familiar with the matter. Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund has agreed to provide roughly $10 billion of the nearly $24 billion. The agreements also include Qatar Investment Authority and Abu Dhabi’s L’imad Holding Co. The commitments by the Middle East funds coincide with the region’s increased economic and political unrest caused by the US and Israel’s war with Iran. Paramount announced its deal to buy Warner Discovery in February. The commitments by the Gulf investors will help offset the cost for the Ellison family and RedBird Capital Partners. The Gulf investors won’t have voting rights in the new Paramount-Warner entity and their involvement is not expected to trigger a mandatory review by US regulators, people familiar with the matter said.

headline: Fashion brand Nykaa sees fastest quarterly revenue growth in 3 yrs
text: Indian fashion-to-beauty retailer Nykaa said it expects net revenue to grow in the late-20% range in the fourth quarter of FY26, its fastest in three years, led by improved fashion sales and steady demand in the beauty segment. The retailer said fourth-quarter consolidated net sales value is expected to grow in the early-30% range, while consolidated gross merchandise value is forecast to rise in the late-20% range.

headline: OpenAI proposes safety nets, grid upgrades for new AI era
text: OpenAI has released policy recommendations to navigate an era of artificial intelligence-fuelled upheaval, including creation of a public wealth fund, fast-response social safety net and speedier electrical grid development. In a document titled Industrial Policy for the Intelligence Age: Ideas to Keep People First, OpenAI proposed policies related to AI superintelligence, referred to as software that can outperform humans in all tasks.

headline: JIIF plans to invest ₹80-100 cr over 12-18 months in early-stage firms
text: Investment platform JITO Incubation and Innovation Foundation said it plans to invest ₹80-100 crore in early-stage startups over the next 12-18 months. The platform has invested over ₹150 crore across more than 100 pre-seed and seed-stage startups over the past two years, and reported more than 15 exits during the period.

headline: UAE’s Valura.ai makes India debut, onboards 1,000 wealth advisors
text: Valura.ai, an AI-native global investment platform, announced the onboarding of over 1,000 wealth advisors across India ahead of its official launch, with a collective assets under management pipeline exceeding ₹3,000 crore in 12-18 months. It provides access to over 100,000 global securities with client assets held in local custody within IFSC at GIFT City under IFSCA regulation.

headline: Sebi eyes initiative to bolster board independence
text: India’s market regulator is working on a collaborative framework with corporates, academia and professional bodies to expand the pipeline and effectiveness of independent directors, even as recent boardroom tensions at HDFC Bank sharpen scrutiny on governance standards. Sebi chief Tuhin Kanta Pandey said the regulator will seek to embark on a joint initiative for capacity building of independent directors at scale with a view to further improve corporate governance. He said boards are well constituted, but not always equally effective, information is available but not always interrogated deeply, and independence exists in form but may not always translate into an independent perspective. The push comes after the abrupt resignation of Atanu Chakraborty as non-executive chairman and independent director of HDFC Bank, which triggered questions about how dissent is expressed and recorded within boards.

headline: Amfi backs intraday loans as Sebi defers rules
text: India’s mutual fund body has asked the market regulator to allow fund houses to use intraday borrowings from banks to purchase securities after Sebi deferred implementation of the new norms to July, according to people aware of the development. On 13 March, Sebi tightened regulations and allowed fund houses to borrow funds from banks on an intraday basis only for repurchase or redemption of units, payment of interest, or income distribution-cum-capital withdrawal payouts to unitholders. Mutual funds said the circular would tie up their hands, and the Association of Mutual Funds in India is in discussions with Sebi. On 25 March, Sebi deferred implementation of the rules to 15 July, citing operational challenges raised by asset management companies.

headline: Titan turns to coloured gems to boost entry-level jewellery
text: India’s top organized jeweller Titan is betting on coloured gemstones to buoy entry-level demand, as volatile gold prices hurt affordability. The firm has launched Hues, a range of coloured gemstone jewellery under its flagship Tanishq label. The collection features over 200 designs crafted from natural stones such as amethyst, tanzanite and tourmaline, and is priced in the ₹40,000-2.5 lakh range, with nearly 70% of the collection carrying a sub-₹2.5 lakh tag. Titan said jewellery demand remains anchored in weddings and festivals, but is increasingly being reshaped by millennials who are keen on lightweight designs, gemstone-led fusion pieces and craftsmanship. Industry executives said there has been a clear move towards coloured gemstones as consumers explore alternatives beyond diamonds and as rarer stones tend to hold and appreciate in value. The launch comes ahead of Akshaya Tritiya, with Titan saying interest in buying jewellery remains high across investment buyers, value seekers and design-led consumers.

headline: Sobha sees record pre-sales in FY26. Is there room for growth?
text: After reporting a pre-sales drop in FY25, realty firm Sobha exited FY26 with a bang. Pre-sales or bookings rose 30% year-on-year to ₹8,136 crore, its best ever, driven by new launches and geographical diversification, though it missed the ₹8,500 crore target set for the year. Sobha launched nine projects in six cities during FY26 and entered Mumbai and Greater Noida. The Gurugram project spillover to FY27 due to delay in RERA approval held back sales. Bengaluru remained the key driver, contributing 55% of total pre-sales. The National Capital Region contributed 30%, while Kerala added 10%. Sobha sold around 5.5 million square feet of space, up 18.5% year-on-year, and average realization rose 9% to ₹14,675 per square feet. Despite the positives and a healthy balance sheet, the stock is down 16% so far in 2026 as investor sentiment has turned sour for realty stocks amid concerns that AI-led disruption and the West Asia war fuelling inflation could dampen housing demand, especially in the mid-income and premium segments.

headline: Marico steady amid uncertainty
text: The humble coconut has emerged as an unlikely buffer for Marico, even as war-led disruption and cost pressures are set to lash its FMCG peers. The Nifty FMCG index is down 16% so far in 2026, while Marico’s stock has been largely flat. The key driver is copra prices, a core input for the maker of Parachute hair oil, which have fallen about 35% from their peak and are expected to remain range-bound in the months ahead. That decline offers Marico a cushion against input inflation triggered by the West Asia conflict, giving it relatively stronger earnings visibility than peers. Copra accounts for roughly half of Marico’s raw material basket, while crude derivatives including packaging form a lower proportion than at many peers. Marico said it expects its gross margin to increase sequentially in the March quarter thanks to easing copra prices, marking a second straight quarterly improvement. Continued brand building investments would still mean double-digit year-on-year growth in Ebitda in the quarter. The company said its consolidated revenue for the quarter grew in the low-20s year-on-year, enabling it to meet its FY26 aspiration of mid-20s revenue growth. Foods business delivered high-teens value growth, while the international business saw high-teens constant currency growth, except the Gulf region which was impacted by the war. Marico’s valuations remain high, and any slowdown in foods or premium personal care could temper investor sentiment.

headline: Stock-pickers gain in muted year for BFSI
text: India’s banking, financial services and insurance sector may have had a muted year on the surface, but a closer look tells a different story. FY26, marked by global uncertainty, earnings downgrades and foreign investor outflows, did not reward broad sector bets but strongly rewarded stock-pickers. A Mint analysis of 724 BFSI stocks shows that more than 18% of the universe generated returns of more than 25% during the year, even as the Nifty Bank and Nifty Financial Services indices fell. The divergence highlights a shift in market behaviour from sector-driven rallies to company-specific performance. MCX surged 124%, LKP Finance gained 112%, while RBL Bank and L&T Finance rose strongly, driven by individual factors such as earnings recovery, improving asset quality or business-specific triggers. At the same time, losses were equally widespread and market capitalization of the BFSI universe fell to ₹94.6 trillion from ₹96.3 trillion. The underlying performance of the BFSI sector remained relatively strong, with revenue and profit growth in Q3FY26 among the best within India Inc. But that did not translate into a re-rating in the market because of valuation pressure, earnings downgrades in select pockets and persistent selling by foreign investors. One of the defining trends of FY26 was the sharp divergence between PSU and private sector banks. Public sector banks outperformed on improving balance sheets, better asset quality and earnings upgrades, while the Nifty Private Bank index declined.

headline: Vedanta fails to stall Adani’s JAL plan at SC
text: The Supreme Court on Monday refused to stay implementation of Adani Enterprises’ ₹14,543 crore resolution plan for bankrupt Jaiprakash Associates, rejecting a challenge by Vedanta. A bench led by the Chief Justice declined to interfere with orders of the National Company Law Tribunal and the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal, which had cleared the way for the plan’s rollout. However, the court directed the panel overseeing the resolution to seek prior NCLAT approval before taking any major steps and asked the appellate tribunal to hear the matter expeditiously. Vedanta, the losing bidder, challenged the lenders’ approval of Adani’s plan and alleged that its higher offer was ignored and the process lacked fairness and transparency. During the hearing, Vedanta argued that its bid offered better value to creditors and that once the plan was implemented and over 15,000 creditors were paid, reversing the process, including delisting, would be difficult. The Committee of Creditors countered that nothing irreversible would happen immediately and that Adani’s plan was superior on merits, particularly in terms of faster upfront payments.

headline: JSW Group pumps ₹2,600 cr in auto arm ahead of launch
text: Billionaire Sajjan Jindal-led JSW Group has so far infused about ₹2,600 crore into its automobile subsidiary, JSW Green Mobility, since inception—signalling a serious push into India’s passenger and commercial vehicle market as it gears up for a FY27 debut. According to filings, the capital was deployed primarily toward setting up plant operations for the passenger and commercial vehicle businesses in Chhatrapati Sambhaji Nagar, alongside general corporate purposes and debt repayment. JSW’s foray will centre on clean fuel technologies such as electric vehicles and hybrids. The group is scheduled to launch its first passenger vehicle in FY27. Experts said the company is likely to front-load investments to build a full-fledged ecosystem rather than scale gradually. JSW Green Mobility is separate from the group’s investment in JSW MG Motor India, the joint venture with SAIC. The automobile business is housed under JSW Green Mobility through two subsidiaries—JSW Motors for passenger vehicles and JSW Greentech for commercial vehicles. JSW Greentech has already secured approval from ARAI for its electric bus.

headline: Dealers flag delays in automobile deliveries
text: The Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations on Monday flagged delays in vehicle deliveries from automakers across the commercial, passenger and two-wheeler segments—the first sign of supply disruption in India’s auto industry due to the US-Iran war. In its near-term outlook, the dealers’ body said that over half of the auto dealers it surveyed reported supply-side challenges owing to the war, with the impact most evident on commercial vehicles. Fada said 53.2% of dealers have experienced some form of supply or dispatch disruption linked to the conflict, with 17.1% reporting significant delays of three or more weeks. The impact on dealer inventories could worsen if the situation does not resolve in the next few weeks, it warned. Fada said consumer purchasing decisions remain unaffected for now, but dealers are urging customers to expedite purchases amid concerns over potential production disruptions.

headline: Luxury hotels leveraging their brands in new vistas
text: India’s luxury hotel chains such as Taj, Marriott, Leela, Oberoi and Sarovar are exploring ways to capitalize on their brands by going beyond room bookings and into branded residences and serviced apartments to diversify their offerings. The trend gathered pace in FY26, with at least half a dozen projects signed and launched across Mumbai, Gurugram, Noida and Greater Noida as hospitality firms eyed more asset-light revenue streams tied to real estate. Indian Hotels recently signed a pact to manage Taj serviced apartments in Noida alongside a five-star hotel project. Branded residences are privately owned homes linked to a hotel brand, offering concierge and other services, while serviced apartments are fully managed and operated much like a hotel. Hotel companies can earn an upfront fee for branding a residential development, in addition to recurring income from management and services in both these and serviced apartment formats. Industry executives said developers are increasingly selling individual units while using a hotel brand to market the project and, in some cases, operate it. Sarovar has signed projects in Greater Noida and Ghaziabad. Roseate entered into a partnership with M3M Group for branded residences at Trump Tower in Gurugram. Consultants said branded residences open up a new revenue stream beyond rooms, allowing hotel firms to stay asset-light while developers can command significantly higher prices than for non-branded homes.

headline: Refineries to put maintenance on hold amid Iran war
text: State-run refineries will delay their maintenance schedules due to the ongoing war in West Asia and the resulting supply constraints. To ensure a stable and continued supply of fuels, refineries of Indian Oil and Bharat Petroleum have postponed routine maintenance shutdowns at some of their facilities, the petroleum ministry said. Delaying refinery maintenance becomes critical as India needs a regular domestic supply of liquefied petroleum gas, which is in short supply amid the war, and because petrol and diesel demand is increasing at a record growth pace every year. All refineries are operating at high capacity with adequate crude inventories, while sufficient stocks of petrol and diesel are being maintained and domestic LPG production has been increased to support domestic consumption. However, Nayara Energy’s Vadinar refinery will move ahead with its planned 35-day maintenance citing unavoidable circumstances and safety issues. Domestic LPG production has dipped slightly because of changes in refinery configuration, but the government said there is sufficient quantity to meet demand.

headline: LPG crisis triggers labour crunch; hiring cost up 15%
text: Staffing firms have reported a 10-15% rise in hiring costs over a month, while hiring agents closely track labour demand trends in the consumer, banking and construction industries. Staffing firm TeamLease said the costs of getting workforce in the metros have gone up by about 15-20% in a month in manufacturing and supply chain sectors. Scarcity of cooking gas has forced blue-collar workers such as scaffolders, plumbers, welders and labourers engaged by the construction and manufacturing sectors back to their home towns and villages. Migrant workers in Mumbai said the price of a cylinder had shot up sharply, pushing many neighbours who work as labourers to return to their villages. Upcoming assembly polls in Assam, Kerala, West Bengal and Tamil Nadu are another push factor for some workers, staffing firms said. The labour supply crunch comes even as many blue-collar workers’ plans to work in West Asia are disrupted by the war. Support platforms for migrant workers said rising LPG costs are pushing labourers to depend on purchased food instead of cooking themselves. Developers in Mumbai, Delhi-NCR and Pune have also reported a dip in labour supply and said labour costs have already risen 5-15% because of the demand-supply mismatch. Some staffing firms are taking fortnightly reviews instead of monthly ones to understand changes in demand, while others are investing more in staff welfare, retention and incentives.

headline: IPL advertisement mix gets a healthy makeover this season
text: The Indian Premier League’s advertising mix is undergoing a shift, with pharmaceutical and wellness brands entering a play dominated by impulse-driven products such as soft drinks and mouth fresheners. Data from TAM Sports shows healthcare as a standout new category, even as most additions are extensions of existing electronics and FMCG segments. The shift signals a broader repositioning of IPL advertising from indulgence-led consumption to health-conscious messaging, as brands work on changing buyer preferences and embedding wellness into mass-market narratives. The IPL advertising pool, pegged at ₹4,900-5,200 crore, has traditionally been dominated by FMCG and consumer electronics players. Sun Pharmaceutical Industries has signed a three-year principal sponsorship and health partnership with Royal Challengers Bengaluru, the first such direct association between a major drugmaker and an IPL franchise. Within the constraints of Indian healthcare advertising rules, brands are aligning health messaging with the IPL’s performance-driven context. Colgate-Palmolive India has partnered with Mumbai Indians as its Dental Performance Partner and launched an oral health screening initiative that links dental metrics to athletic performance. Supplement brands are also leaning into team affiliations and co-branded products.

headline: Iran rejects ceasefire as Trump amps up threats
text: Iran on Monday rejected a 45-day ceasefire proposal and said it wants a permanent end to the war, even as Israel attacked a major gas field and US President Donald Trump’s ultimatum to open the Strait of Hormuz loomed. Iran said it would accept only an end to the war with guarantees that it would not be attacked again, and conveyed its response through Pakistan, a mediator. Trump later stepped up his threats against Iran, saying the entire country could be taken out in one night. Iranian and Omani officials were working on a mechanism for administering the Strait of Hormuz, through which a fifth of the world’s oil is shipped in peacetime. Iran has refused to let US and Israeli vessels through after they started the war on 28 February. Iran’s rejection came after Israel struck a key petrochemical plant in the South Pars natural gas field and killed two Revolutionary Guard commanders. The gas field attack aimed at eliminating a major source of revenue for Iran, Israel said. Brent crude oil rose in early trading before wavering. Explosions boomed in Tehran and Israeli forces said they struck three Tehran airports overnight. Iran also kept up pressure on Gulf neighbours, including strikes on infrastructure. The ongoing war has killed thousands across Iran and Lebanon and displaced large numbers of people.

headline: A downed airman, a mountain hideout and a high-risk rescue in Iran
text: For nearly two days, injured and alone, a US aviator hid in a remote mountain crevice as Iranian forces and militias closed in on him with helicopters and drones. Early Sunday, he heard the roar of US aircraft and a barrage of fire as US commandos reached him deep inside Iran. As they whisked him to safety, they blew up aircraft stranded on the ground rather than risk sophisticated military equipment falling into Iranian hands. The aviator had been one of two crew flying in an F-15E Strike Eagle when it was shot down by Iranian forces on Friday. A US military team quickly rescued the pilot, but the other crew member who flew in the back seat of the fighter as a weapons-systems officer went missing. The effort to recover the officer set off a sprawling rescue mission involving around 100 special-operations forces, dozens of warplanes and helicopters and a last-minute CIA deception campaign to buy more time. Four B-1 bombers reportedly dropped dozens of satellite-guided bombs while drones struck suspected fighters approaching the hiding site. The operation ran into problems, with helicopters taking small-arms fire and transport aircraft getting stuck in a makeshift forward base inside Iran. The CIA helped pinpoint the aviator’s location and spread false word inside Iran about the rescue route to throw trackers off. After the mission was complete, the US destroyed the aircraft left behind so their technology would not be compromised.

headline: Jamie Dimon warns of higher inflation, interest rates from Iran war
text: JPMorgan Chase chief executive Jamie Dimon warned that the war in Iran could push up inflation and drag down financial markets further if interest rates start to rise. In his annual letter to shareholders, Dimon said there is a risk of more oil and commodity price shocks in the months ahead, which could lead to prolonged inflation and ultimately higher interest rates. He noted how rapid increases in oil prices helped cause large recessions in the 1970s and 1980s, though the US is less vulnerable to those types of shocks today. Dimon also said the outcome of conflicts between the world’s great powers, including the wars in Ukraine and Iran, is more important than the financial or economic impacts they might bring. He offered advice on regulation and private credit, saying many private credit providers will fare worse than others in a downturn and that selling such products to retail investors requires greater transparency and higher standards.

headline: Israeli airstrike kills at least 10 people near Gaza school
text: An Israeli airstrike killed at least 10 people and wounded several others outside a school housing displaced Palestinians in central Gaza, health officials said. Before the strikes, some Palestinians had clashed with members of an Israeli-backed militia, who they said attacked the school in an attempt to abduct people. In the midst of the clashes east of the Maghazi refugee camp, Israeli drones fired two missiles into the area. It was not immediately clear how many civilians had been killed in the strikes, which hit a densely packed neighbourhood of mostly displaced Palestinians.

headline: Silver up ₹5,000, gold ₹2,300 as dollar dips
text: Silver prices jumped ₹5,000 to ₹2.42 lakh per kilogram in the national capital on Monday, while gold advanced to ₹1.53 lakh per 10 grams due to easing crude oil rates and a weak US dollar. According to the All India Sarafa Association, silver rose 2.11% from Friday’s closing level and gold of 99.9% purity advanced 1.52%. Analysts said bullion prices recovered amid value buying following the recent decline in precious metals. HDFC Securities said precious metals are expected to remain sensitive to geopolitical developments in West Asia, which will continue to play a crucial role in shaping market direction in domestic markets.

headline: Indian firms’ NDF trading surges 7x
text: Indian companies’ activity in the non-deliverable forwards market surged to over $7 billion on 30 March, around seven times the average, signalling a rush to capture arbitrage opportunities created by banks unwinding positions following regulatory curbs. The unwinding followed the Reserve Bank of India’s restrictions on lenders’ net onshore open FX positions, prompting a rush to lower positions aimed at benefiting from gaps between onshore and non-deliverable forwards. Client trading volumes in the NDF market jumped to $7.54 billion on 30 March, compared with the average monthly volume, according to Clearing Corp. of India data.

headline: Jindal Steel deploys syngas in furnaces
text: Jindal Steel said it has deployed syngas in galvanizing and colour coating line furnaces to counter the shortage of natural gas, LPG and propane, enabling the company to sustain operations amid supply disruptions. Syngas, or synthesis gas, is a clean-burning fuel that offers a way to convert waste and biomass into valuable energy. The switch to syngas—produced through gasification of coal—has allowed the company to mitigate fuel constraints in these critical finishing processes, where high-temperature furnaces are essential for applying zinc and colour coatings to steel strips used in construction, appliances and automotive sectors. Jindal Steel said the integrated deployment of syngas across its steelmaking value chain sets a benchmark for efficiency, sustainability and energy self-reliance.

headline: Tonse takes over as Yes Bank MD & CEO
text: Yes Bank said Vinay Muralidhar Tonse has taken charge as managing director and chief executive officer of the bank for three years. Tonse, a former managing director of State Bank of India, replaced Prashant Kumar, who completed his extended term on 5 April. Tonse has more than three and a half decades of experience spanning treasury, retail banking, corporate banking, international operations and asset management. During his stint as an SBI managing director, he had responsibility for the lender’s domestic network of nearly 23,000 branches and business levels of ₹76 trillion as of 30 November 2025.

headline: GCPL sees hit if oil prices remain high
text: Godrej Consumer Products said it expects costs to rise 6% to 9% if Brent crude holds at $100 to $110 a barrel and palm oil prices remain elevated. Recent gains in both commodities have been driven by the ongoing West Asia war. Palm oil derivatives, a key input for soaps and personal care products, along with crude-linked packaging and freight costs, are key expenses for consumer companies. The maker of Cinthol soaps and Goodknight mosquito repellent said it expects to offset the impact of cost increases through price hikes and other savings measures.

headline: Rupee records biggest surge in 12 years
text: The Indian rupee edged up, extending its biggest rally in 12 years after the central bank doubled down on curbing speculation against the local currency. The rupee closed 0.1% higher at 93.0612 per dollar after rising as much as 0.4%. The currency had rallied 1.8% in the previous session, the most since September 2013. The rupee swung sharply after the Reserve Bank of India unleashed measures to restrict banks in the onshore forward market. The unit had been hitting successive lows despite repeated intervention, with pressure intensifying after the Iran war drove up India’s fuel import costs. Analysts said the rupee may gain further as banks unwind their dollar positions ahead of the 10 April deadline.

headline: Indices rebound as crude oil softens
text: Benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty staged a sharp rebound after falling in early trade following a correction in crude oil prices amid reports of ceasefire efforts in the West Asia war. Intense buying in banking and IT stocks, and a strengthening rupee, supported investor sentiment. In a volatile session, the Sensex jumped 787.30 points to settle at 74,106.85, while the Nifty edged higher by 255.15 points to end at 22,968.25.

headline: India adds record wind capacity
text: India has achieved the highest-ever annual wind energy capacity addition of 6.05 GW in 2025-26, taking cumulative installed capacity to over 56 GW, the ministry of new and renewable energy said. The milestone reflects renewed momentum in the sector, driven by improved policy clarity, transmission readiness, competitive tariff discovery and a strong project pipeline.

headline: Wilson resigns as Air India CEO, on notice period
text: Air India chief executive Campbell Wilson has stepped down from the helm of India’s second-largest airline and is currently serving his notice period, according to people with direct knowledge of the matter. The Tata Group had hired Wilson from Singapore Airlines’ low-cost unit Scoot in May 2022, less than four months after acquiring the government-run airline for ₹18,000 crore. His tenure was to end in July 2027. Following the acquisition, the Tata Group merged Vistara with Air India and Singapore Airlines became a shareholder in Air India. In Wilson’s third year at the airline, things took a turn for the worse after an Air India flight from Ahmedabad to London crashed shortly after takeoff in June 2025. Subsequently, increased scrutiny, inspections and a temporary grounding of several aircraft strained operations. The India-Pakistan conflict and the war in West Asia added further pressure by raising fuel costs, extending flight durations and limiting viable routes. Four years into its turnaround under Tata ownership, Air India’s aircraft retrofit programme is two years behind schedule, slowing fleet upgrades and international expansion. In FY25, Air India’s standalone revenue rose 13% to ₹61,080 crore and standalone losses narrowed to ₹3,976 crore. Borrowings excluding lease liabilities stood at ₹29,713 crore at the end of FY25.

headline: Why IPOs no longer feel like easy wins
text: For many retail investors, the IPO narrative has subtly changed. The frenzy that once fuelled easy listing gains appears to have faded as market conditions turned less supportive. Investors who once saw initial public offerings as quick wins are increasingly facing muted listings, weaker post-listing returns and greater downside. The war in West Asia has begun to weigh on the primary market as well, with companies such as PhonePe deferring listing plans citing geopolitical tensions, market volatility and the need for greater liquidity. XED Executive Development, which had aimed to become the first GIFT City IPO, also withdrew its offer despite meeting minimum subscription levels because of volatile markets, tight liquidity and the risk of post-listing pressure. Market participants say issuers are becoming more sensitive to valuation expectations, post-listing performance and market stability. Historically, the bar for IPOs rises during market drawdowns, with fewer issues coming and valuations getting derated. Domestic institutional flows have slowed and global investors remain in selloff mode, restricting demand for new paper. Data shows that the era of easy gains in IPOs fuelled by the post-2020 liquidity wave is beginning to fade. Average one-year returns for NSE mainboard IPOs in 2025 were just 3.03%, compared with a peak of 106.54% in 2020. The number of mainboard IPOs trading above their issue price one year after listing plunged to four in 2025 from a peak of 52 in 2024. SME IPOs tell a similar story. Market participants say the cycle has shifted from a liquidity-driven rally to a more selective, risk-aware phase where business quality, earnings visibility and valuation discipline matter more. Many issuers are now in wait-and-watch mode, choosing to let approvals lapse or delay launches rather than risk entering a volatile or bearish market.

headline: Rate pause likely as war clouds inflation, growth
text: As the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) heads into its first policy decision of the new financial year on 8 April, a rate pause is widely expected even as a rapidly shifting macro landscape triggered by the West Asia war may force a shift in its outlook. A Mint poll of 10 economists and market participants points to rising inflation risks and a weakening growth outlook, with all expecting the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) to hold rates while signalling a more cautious policy stance. In 2025, the RBI had cumulatively cut the repo rate—the rate at which it lends short-term funds to banks—by 125 basis points (bps), with the last cut of 25 bps in December to 5.25%. ‘We do expect RBI to hold onto the repo rate and stance,’ said Madan Sabnavis, chief economist at Bank of Baroda. The MPC’s stance has remained neutral since June 2025. ‘The tone will be cautious,’ Sabnavis added. ‘(Gross Domestic Product or GDP) growth forecast is important as it will anchor market expectations—it could be in the range of 7-7.25%, inflation around 4-4.5%.’ Separately, experts do not expect the RBI to use policy rates to shore up the rupee, which has been under pressure since the war began, as the central bank has already taken a series of external and regulatory measures to manage volatility. Meanwhile, markets are keenly watching the RBI’s projections on economic growth and inflation. In its previous policy on 6 February, the MPC had projected real GDP growth for April-June quarter at 6.9% and July-September at 7%, and had deferred the projections for the full year to the April policy because of the new GDP series released in February. As for inflation, the RBI projected consumer price index (CPI) inflation at 4% and 4.2% for Q1 FY27 and Q2, respectively. CPI inflation rose to 3.21% in February from 2.75% in January. A 5 April report by SBI Research said the war has triggered ‘the largest disruption to the global oil market… since 1973’, pushing up imported inflation and weakening the rupee. Brent crude prices have surged to more than $100 per barrel from $73.91 on 27 February, a day before the war began. ‘Before the war, we were looking at inflation of 4.1%, and now we are expecting it at 4.7% but with an upward bias,’ Upasana Bharadwaj, economist at Kotak Mahindra Bank said, adding that the bank’s GDP growth estimate has been revised down from 7% to 6.5% in the new financial year. HDFC Bank also echoed similar concerns. ‘We may see an upward revision in the CPI forecast given the impact on prices already visible in March,’ Sakshi Gupta, principal economist at HDFC Bank said. However, she expects the RBI to stress that inflation remains within its target band. Barclays, too, has pegged FY27 GDP growth at 6.8% and inflation at 4%, warning that a prolonged oil shock could push inflation above target and slow growth further. A key theme this time is the RBI’s proactive defence of the rupee, even as market participants do not expect fresh measures in the policy itself. Recent steps—from limits on banks’ currency positions to curbs in the derivatives market—signal an aggressive approach, tightening offshore rupee regulations to curb speculation and limit spillovers to the onshore market. Despite the rupee hitting an all-time low of 95.1250 per dollar on 30 March, most experts believe policy action and currency management will remain separate. ‘I don’t think policy will have measures for currency. Those are done on how the central bank views volatility,’ Sabnavis said. Bharadwaj added that RBI has already taken several measures to curb speculative activity against the rupee, ‘and any of the measures don’t have to be linked to policy’. Expectations are that the RBI will continue with regulatory and unconventional tools rather than rate hikes to defend the currency, Tanay Dalal, senior vice president II – business & economic research at Axis Bank said. Despite intervention, pressure on the rupee is expected to persist. Barclays estimates USD/INR could weaken toward 96.8 by December 2026, reflecting a widening current account deficit and global headwinds. In the bond market, yields are likely to remain elevated as risk premia rise. MUFG expects India’s 10-year yield to stay biased further above 7% amid fiscal concerns and global factors. Liquidity management will also be key, with the RBI likely to rely on tools such as VRR and VRRR to keep conditions broadly neutral while managing borrowing pressures. Overall, the April policy is shaping up to be less about action and more about signalling in an increasingly uncertain global environment. ‘The uncertainty around the impact of the current conflict could keep the RBI in a wait-and-watch mode,’ HDFC Bank’s Gupta said.

headline: TCS grapples with top talent erosion
text: Tata Consultancy Services Ltd (TCS) was long revered as one of the safest private-sector employers. But layoffs driven by an artificial intelligence-powered upheaval and deep cuts to variable payouts have shaken confidence, sparking an unprecedented exodus at the top. At least 300 of 1,800 senior executives have quit India’s largest software services provider in eight months through 31 March, representing at least 16% churn among senior ranks, the highest since the company went public in 2004, according to three executives familiar with the exits. This category witnessed 4-5% annual churn earlier, they said. Executives with over two decades of experience, including principal consultants, vice presidents, and senior vice presidents, have resigned during this period, said the people who didn’t want to be identified. Mint could not independently determine how many of these 300 executives were among those laid off. TCS had kicked off its largest job cuts, removing 12,000 executives or 2% of its workforce, as AI disrupted India’s $297-billion technology services outsourcing industry. TCS has been undergoing significant restructuring and has also started to edge away from its lifetime employment commitment, said Peter Bendor-Samuel, founder of Everest Group. ‘The combination of these effects has created increased uncertainty and some dissatisfaction. Some specific clients may feel the impact as their favoured consultants and engineers are no longer with the account.’ Queries emailed to TCS went unanswered until press time. ‘The thing top-most on the minds of the people is why we are doing this. We do not pay the best. Yet we managed to attract some of the best minds because of brand Tata. We always promised the best opportunities to people, a wide variety of projects in which they could work,’ said one of the executives cited earlier. ‘That trust has been broken.’ TCS, which saw 13.5% attrition in the December quarter, once had the lowest exit rate among peers. But that gap has narrowed. Cognizant, Infosys and HCL Technologies ended the quarter with voluntary attrition of 13.9%, 12.3% and 12.4%, respectively. A high exit rate among senior executives raises questions about the company’s future, as these executives are the cornerstone of its flawless project execution. ‘No AI bots or automation tools can replace this talent pool,’ said another executive. ‘Obviously, it does not bode well for the company.’ Amit Chandra, vice-president at HDFC Securities, said TCS’s growth has been impacted despite strong deal wins because of higher leakages, and the layoffs have created a sense of instability. TCS lost some work from large customers including Zurich Life Insurance to DXC Technology last year and the UK insurance giant Phoenix Group to Wipro. In October, TCS lost a $585 million contract from Paramount Global to LTIMindtree. The firm reported $22.4 billion in revenue during April-December, implying it needs 3.65% dollar revenue growth in January-March to match its FY25 full-year revenue of $30.18 billion. Achieving this sequential growth is particularly difficult during a seasonally weak quarter, increasing the possibility that TCS may report a full-year revenue decline. A weak macro environment adds to the uncertainty, prompting large firms to hold back on tech spending. A second reason for departures is that the senior leadership pool has not received more than 10% of variable pay over the past two years, according to executives. Many of these executives subsequently joined startups, Fortune 500 companies or smaller firms like Genpact, offering higher compensation. ‘For more than two years, none of this senior leadership has received any variable pay, even as the company has paid hikes and variable pay to the junior staff,’ said another executive. Some analysts said the shift is structural. ‘This is less about layoffs and more about a structural reset. When firms move from labour-led delivery to AI-led execution, you simply need fewer layers of senior oversight,’ said Phil Fersht, chief executive of HFS Research. Thomas Reuner of Pierre Audoin Consultants said the direction of travel is toward fewer middle layers and more senior positions that can handle execution and coordination. High churn in the senior leadership ranks, along with declining growth, came at a time when TCS shares hit a six-year low late last month.

headline: Tempting customers to deposit remains a tough task for lenders
text: Getting customers to park their money in deposits remains a struggle for banks, as loan demand continues to race ahead of deposit growth. In the March quarter, HDFC Bank stood out as the sole lender to raise deposits faster than loans, a period when its peers struggled. Early business updates from 19 banks, excluding small finance banks, showed that only a few managed to shrink the gap between loan and deposit growth. One of them was state-owned Bank of Baroda, which reported 12% growth in deposits and 16.2% growth in loans, against 10.3% and 14.7% respectively in the December quarter. At HDFC Bank, deposits grew 14.4%, while loans expanded at 12% in Q4 of FY26, as against 11.6% and 11.9% in the December quarter. Analysts said these numbers would assuage investor concerns raised by the abrupt exit of its part-time chairman Atanu Chakraborty. Analysts at Sanford C Bernstein said the provisional numbers would be reassuring for investors who assess the bank’s performance on metrics such as headline deposit growth and loan-deposit ratio. The provisional data also showed that the gap between deposit and credit growth widened for many banks over the past quarter. For instance, IDFC First Bank’s deposit growth was 300 bps above credit growth in Q3, which reversed to a 280 bps deficit in the March quarter. Bandhan Bank’s deposit growth was 120 bps over its credit growth in Q3, but in Q4 credit grew 260 bps higher than deposits. Some of this is due to the stronger credit growth in the last quarter of the financial year, when banks see higher demand for many loans. Deposit-raising has been a problem for quite some time now. Savvier investors are drawn towards the equity markets, directly or through mutual funds that have amped up awareness campaigns. However, with equity markets under pressure over the last year as well as the current volatility owing to the West Asia war, it would be interesting to see whether some investors return to the banking system. The overall banking system saw a loan growth of 13.7% and deposit growth of 10.8% in FY26 up to 15 March, RBI data showed. Despite concerns that the war could cause an economic slump and slow down credit demand, analysts remain upbeat. Motilal Oswal said the momentum remains robust, supported by liquidity buffers and a consumption-led recovery following GST cuts, and systemic credit growth could sustain at 13.5% year-on-year in FY27. These analysts also said that while system-wide deposit growth stood stable at 10.8%, faster credit growth has led to a spike in the credit-deposit ratio to 83%. With competition for deposits remaining intense, banks continue to face challenges in mobilizing low-cost deposits, and term deposit rates are expected to remain sticky.

headline: Centre revives ‘Go Electric’ with 2-wheeler firms
text: The West Asia war-triggered energy supply shocks are pushing India to speed up shift to electric mobility to cut its oil import dependence. Towards this, the Bureau of Energy Efficiency started consultations with electric two-wheeler makers on 2 April, as it looks to rev up its five-year-old ‘Go Electric’ campaign, two people aware of the matter said. The idea is to build micro-level awareness on electric vehicle benefits to stir demand. Two-wheelers are central to India’s green energy push as they use a bulk of the country’s petrol. They guzzled nearly two-third of the total petrol consumption of 38.8 million tonnes in FY26. Amid the war uncertainties, Prime Minister Narendra Modi on 27 March exhorted states to push for alternative fuels and electric mobility. India is the world’s third largest energy buyer after the US and China. The US-Iran war has disrupted shipments via the Strait of Hormuz, through which about 30% of India’s oil cargoes move. In this light, BEE will lead the effort to leverage and revive India’s ‘Go Electric’ campaign. This was first launched amid the pandemic-led disruptions in February 2021. The Centre’s push to assist states in raising awareness about e-mobility comes in the backdrop of pressure on state-run oil marketing companies. Indian Oil, Bharat Petroleum and Hindustan Petroleum have hiked prices of premium petrol and diesel on global cues, but have kept prices of regular fuels unchanged. Private OMCs Nayara Energy and Shell have hiked fuel prices. ‘There was a meeting on 2 April, wherein two-wheeler industry stakeholders were called by the BEE to discuss the campaign,’ said the first person, adding that the meet was attended by Ather Energy, Ola Electric and Hero MotoCorp, among others. The meeting did not include carmakers, as these EVs are sold at a higher price point, making immediate adoption a challenge. The discussion centred around ways to reduce people’s apprehension around EVs, especially those related to safety and uncertainty around new technology. There were discussions around reaching out to resident welfare associations to run awareness campaigns and offer test rides, and using digital as well as billboard marketing. Queries sent to the BEE, the power ministry and vehicle makers remained unanswered. Energy security experts said it is important to move towards e-mobility and reduce dependence on oil. Kirit Parikh said there may be range anxiety or concerns over the initial cost because of charging infrastructure and battery prices, but those concerns can be addressed. India’s adoption of electric mobility is on the rise and costs are coming down. A December 2025 report by KPMG said India has almost achieved price parity between the total cost of buying and operating an electric two-wheeler and a petrol-run one. Petrol two-wheeler sales topped 11 million units in FY26, but were still lower than the FY22 level of 13.2 million. Electric two-wheeler sales rose to 1.4 million in FY26 from 252,787 in FY22, per Vahan data. The ‘Go Electric’ campaign had been launched by the road transport and highways, power, and new and renewable energy ministries to reduce crude oil dependence by promoting e-mobility and electric cookstoves. Mint had reported on 3 April that the government was looking to boost output of induction stoves to push electricity-based cooking amid the energy crisis.

headline: Builders reel as workers pack up amid gas crisis
text: India’s real estate sector is facing a shortage of skilled workers and rising labour costs, as soaring cooking gas prices push migrant workers back home, even as larger developers appear better placed to manage the disruption. Developers across Mumbai, Delhi-NCR and Pune said the spike in liquefied petroleum gas prices, along with supply constraints linked to the West Asia conflict, has raised the cost of living for migrant workers, triggering a dip in labour availability across key property markets. Labour costs have already risen 5-15% due to the demand-supply mismatch, developers estimated, with the long-term impact likely to be more severe. ‘We are witnessing a real and immediate labour disruption, particularly over March and early April,’ said Vishal Agarwal of Pune-based Krisala Developers, adding that many migrant workers, especially bachelors and contract labour, are finding it difficult to sustain themselves in cities due to lack of access to affordable cooking fuel and food. He said larger, organized projects with in-house facilities have been relatively more stable, but the broader ecosystem is under pressure. Rohit Gupta of Pune-based Mantra Group said while the broader real estate industry is feeling the pinch of the labour shortage, his company has been able to cushion the impact to a large extent by focusing on on-site worker welfare, ensuring basic amenities and maintaining strong contractor relationships. The concerns over migrant workers have emerged at a time when India’s real estate sector is witnessing a construction boom, as housing, commercial office and hospitality industries have been on a high. In high-growth markets, where housing demand is strong, the imbalance between demand and available skilled labour is even more pronounced. ‘There has been a noticeable increase in labour costs. Skilled labour, in particular, has seen an escalation of approximately 8-10%, driven by supply constraints, higher cost of living, and intermittent disruptions in construction activity,’ said Niranjan Hiranandani, chairman of Naredco and founder and chairman of Hiranandani Communities. He added that supply-side disruptions in key construction inputs such as fuel, tiles and allied materials have impacted site-level activity. Sachin Bhandari of VTP Realty said lack of sufficient manpower may delay construction and completion of projects in the long run. Real estate firms typically procure manpower from contractors, who are now forced to retain labour at higher costs. Amit Mamgain of Gurugram-headquartered Yugen Infra said while labourers are moving back to their hometowns due to a spike in the cost of living, contractor networks and other labour supply channels can manage workforce requirements within the industry. The impact may vary depending on developer size and location. Hiranandani said labour shortages can lead to execution delays, cost escalations and pressure on project timelines. Organized developers are mitigating this through better planning and mechanization, but the broader impact on delivery schedules across the sector is evident.

headline: Bars, eateries whip up IPL menus while LPG disruption bites
text: India’s restaurants, bars and quick-service chains are seeing a much-needed rebound after the Indian Premier League season 19 kicked off on 28 March, with match screenings, group dining and delivery driving sales over weekends. After a soft start to March due to the LPG supply crunch caused by the West Asia war, the tournament has brought some respite to eateries. For hospitality businesses, the 84-match calendar overlaps with the summer months, offering a sustained consumption trigger, turning cricket fandom into higher footfall and bigger orders. The industry expects 5-10% growth on normal match days, and bigger spikes on high-profile game days and weekends. ‘More than anything, the cricket extravaganza is about community and people coming together. In uncertain times, these shared experiences become more meaningful,’ said Rahul Singh of The Beer Café. He said the company did blockbuster business on the opening match weekend and April and May could bring in at least 25% more revenue. Mumbai-based Impresario Entertainment and Hospitality, which runs Social and Smoke House Deli among others, is running a ‘Doosra Stadium’ initiative at its Social bars. The company said it has seen a strong start with an uptick in footfalls and group dining, especially over weekends. The opening weekend of IPL season 19 had two high-scoring games, reaching over 515 million viewers across TV and digital, 26% higher than last season, according to JioStar. In Bengaluru, Handcrafted Restaurants, which runs Helen’s Place and Roxie, said IPL screenings drove a 10-15% jump in footfall over the past 10 days. Match days now deliver roughly a 10% sales uplift at Geist Brewing Co., helped by cricket-themed bundles. ‘Warmer weather, open-air formats and the beer-cricket connection should support stronger sales this season, especially if Bengaluru goes along in the tournament,’ said co-founder Narayan Manepally. For quick-service restaurants, the IPL is just as much about delivery as dine-in. Wow! Momo launched the ‘Indian Momo League’, using city-based fandom and the tournament to drive more frequent orders and higher average bills. ‘IPL should have a good impact on deliveries. March was not particularly strong, but it was not a washout either,’ said co-founder Sagar Daryani. Some brands are also exploring team partnerships and limited-edition products. Curefoods is running a ‘Slice Maar’ campaign with Rajasthan Royals. Indians are also eating out more often, with average dining-out frequency rising from 6.6 times a month in 2019 to 7.9 times in 2024, according to the National Restaurant Association of India. The restaurant industry is expected to reach ₹7.76 trillion by FY28, growing at 8.1% CAGR. The IPL offers a ready-made multi-week occasion that cuts across formats, cities and income groups, allowing bars, casual dining chains and delivery-led brands to chase extra demand.

headline: CII seeks support as war-led supply chain crisis deepens
text: Supply-side pressures arising from the West Asia war continue to persist, and businesses need targeted liquidity support, industry lobby group Confederation of Indian Industry said on Sunday. The next phase of policy response needs to focus on targeted liquidity support, credit facilitation, trade cost management and foreign exchange stability, it said in a statement outlining 20 steps required to address the spillover effects of the war on the Indian economy. Chandrajit Banerjee, director general of CII, said the government’s and the Reserve Bank of India’s early measures have helped stabilize sentiment, underscoring policy responsiveness in the face of external shocks. But the situation continues to evolve, and energy, logistics and trade channels remain under pressure. Several sectors continue to face operational and financial stress, particularly micro, small and medium enterprises, exporters and energy-intensive industries, he added. The lobby group pitched for a credit guarantee scheme, under which collateral-free working capital can be extended to affected businesses through government-backed guarantees, particularly to MSMEs, exporters and gas-dependent sectors. The CII also pitched for a three-month moratorium and restructuring window for MSMEs, especially exporters and ancillary units linked to export supply chains. This may include calibrated flexibility in asset classification rules, with a defined deferment before SMA and NPA recognition is triggered, limited to sectors where disruption is demonstrable. The RBI could institute a special refinance window for small businesses and other affected sectors, complemented by targeted liquidity support, enabling banks and NBFCs to continue extending credit at reasonable cost to productive sectors. The ministry of finance in conjunction with RBI could provide immediate contractual and operational relief to industry, especially MSMEs, by extending delivery timelines for central and state PSU contracts by 3-4 months without invoking liquidated damages clauses and reducing performance bank guarantee and security deposit requirements to minimal levels. In addition, temporary relief in electricity tariffs may also be offered to help manage rising input costs during the disruption period. The proposals are significant because many large businesses depend on MSMEs for raw materials and other inputs. Stress among small businesses could impact larger factories as well. India has a large MSME base, which accounts for about 36% of the country’s manufacturing output and 45% of exports. The sector is also the second-largest employer after agriculture. The CII also sought a cut in import duties on energy inputs to mitigate the cascading cost impacts of the supply chain disruption, including a temporary waiver of the 2.5% customs duty on LNG imports.

headline: Trump risks confidence in US role as guardian of global shipping
text: Of all the things Donald Trump has done to disrupt global commerce, from levying punitive tariffs to tearing up trade deals, few would be as consequential as withdrawing and leaving the rest of the world to secure the Persian Gulf. The move, which the US president has repeatedly threatened as his war with Iran drags on, would represent a break with decades of US policy keeping open the sea lanes that carry four-fifths of the $35 trillion global goods trade. Even the threat of reducing security for the Strait of Hormuz risks shaking confidence in a pillar of the world economy, as well as American wealth and power. Traffic through the strait has dropped to a handful of ships daily from about 135 before the war, with Iran allowing passage mainly for its own exports. Those conditions are putting at risk roughly one-fifth of global oil flows, driving up prices and injecting volatility into energy markets. Since World War II, the US has used its navy to deter attacks, counter piracy and challenge attempts by states to restrict lawful passage across the oceans that cover more than 70% of the Earth’s surface. Those guarantees have allowed oil, goods and commodities to pass across borders with minimal friction. ‘The free flow of commerce through the strait is a larger principle at stake in this conflict,’ said retired vice admiral John W. Miller, former commander of US Fifth Fleet in Bahrain. European and Asian officials told Bloomberg that the conflict has eroded faith in the US role as protector of the high seas, raising concerns about energy prices, shifting security calculations around key choke points and growing doubts about Washington’s ability to manage the consequences of the war. In the absence of a US plan, smaller, trade-dependent nations have sought to build consensus for a multinational response. The UAE urged the United Nations to authorize a range of measures to reopen the strait, and the UK convened representatives from more than 40 American allies to discuss non-military options to convince Tehran to restore trade.

headline: OMCs to cut refinery payouts to curb losses
text: In a first since fuel price deregulation, Indian state-run oil marketing companies will pay refineries a discounted price for petrol, diesel, aviation turbine fuel and kerosene to limit mounting losses from a self-imposed freeze on retail fuel prices, sources said. The oil marketing companies on 26 March fixed rates for petroleum products that are at a discount of up to ₹60 per litre to their imported cost, two people with direct knowledge of the matter said. The discounted rates, applicable with effect from 16 March, will hit standalone refiners such as MRPL, CPCL and HMEL the most. International oil prices have risen from about $70 per barrel before the West Asia war to over $100, but retail petrol and diesel prices in India have remained unchanged, forcing OMCs to absorb the impact. With no immediate end to the conflict in sight, OMCs have decided to fix a discount on the refinery transfer price, the internal price at which refineries sell fuel to marketing arms, to effectively pay refiners less than the import-parity cost of fuels like petrol and diesel. For the second half of March, a discount of ₹22,342 per kilolitre was fixed on diesel to bring down the RTP of ₹85,349 per kl to ₹63,007 per kl. For the first fortnight of April, the discount on diesel has been fixed at ₹60,239 per kl to lower RTP from ₹146,243 per kl to ₹86,004 per kl. On ATF, the RTP has been slashed to ₹76,923 per kl from ₹127,486 per kl after considering a discount of ₹50,564 per kl. The RTP for kerosene after a discount of ₹46,311 per kl has been fixed at ₹77,534 per kl from ₹123,845 per kl, they said.

headline: Food prices stable despite West Asia war
text: The government’s measures have kept prices of essential commodities in India stable, with staples such as rice, wheat, atta and pulses showing a decline over the year and month prior, according to consumer affairs secretary Nidhi Khare. The government is actively monitoring prices of 40 essential commodities daily amid concerns over imported inflation, Khare said. Timely interventions, including buffer stock releases and supply-side steps, prevented sharp spikes despite external shocks, she said. Cereal prices have stayed flat year-on-year as of 4 April. Rice stood at ₹42.61 per kg compared with ₹42.89 a year ago, while wheat declined to ₹31 per kg from ₹31.76. Wheat flour eased to ₹36.98 per kg from ₹37.6, indicating adequate domestic availability and stable procurement. Pulses, a major driver of food inflation in previous years, have shown a broad-based softening. Tur dal declined to ₹122.05 per kg from ₹130.63 a year earlier, gram dal to ₹85.04 from ₹87.59, and urad dal to ₹117.44 from ₹119.18. Moong dal also saw a marginal correction, while masoor dal remained largely stable. Retail inflation rose to a 10-month high of 3.21% in February on costlier vegetables and fresh food security risks. ‘The reason that I see for the price correction is the disruption in exports of commodities such as rice, wheat, wheat products and vegetables. While this is positive from a consumer and inflation perspective, we also need to look at it from the farmers’ point of view,’ said Rakesh Arrawatia of IRMA. On 24 March, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said in Lok Sabha that the Centre had constituted seven empowered groups of officials and experts to assess the impact of the war in West Asia and take remedial measures across sectors. Vegetable prices have moderated sharply over a year earlier as of 4 April. Onion prices dropped to ₹24.99 per kg from ₹31.11, while potato fell to ₹20.42 from ₹23.59. Tomato prices, however, increased to ₹26.76 per kg from ₹20.89.

headline: Govt steps up LPG supply, urges calm
text: The sale of small 5-kg LPG cylinders—available across-the-counter at LPG distributorships on showing valid ID proofs—has been stepped up, with about 660,000 bottles sold since 23 March as the government ramps up supplies to meet demand. Unlike the subsidised domestic 14.2-kg cylinders, the 5-kg bottles, called FTL cylinders, are priced at market rates and do not require any address proof for procurement from a nearby LPG distributorship. ‘Yesterday, more than 90,000 5-kg FTL cylinders were sold. Since March 23, 2026, about 6.6 lakh 5-kg FTL cylinders have been sold,’ the oil ministry said in a statement. It said there are no reports of shortages at LPG distributor points, with more than 5.1 million domestic cylinders delivered during the day and online bookings accounting for 95% of total demand. Authorities have intensified action against hoarding and black marketing, seizing over 50,000 cylinders since March and issuing more than 1,400 show-cause notices to LPG distributors, with 36 dealerships suspended so far. The government has prioritised supplies of domestic LPG and PNG for households, hospitals and educational institutions.

headline: Paragon plans exits as it eyes Fund III with ₹1,500-cr corpus
text: Paragon Partners, which has backed consumer brands such as Chai Point and mCaffeine, has lined up exits for its earlier investments as it prepares to launch its third mid-market private equity fund, targeting a corpus of ₹1,500 crore to continue investing in profitable Indian companies. ‘We received Sebi approval to raise ₹2,000 crore fund, which includes a green shoe option, but our ideal size will be ₹1,200-1,500 crore. That’s the sweet spot where we can maintain return discipline while pursuing the kind of opportunities we want to do in the mid-market space,’ co-founder and senior partner Siddharth Parekh told Mint. It will begin fundraising in next few months and expects to do a final close in a 12-18 month horizon. ‘Beyond capital raising and deployment, we’ll spend considerable time securing liquidity via exits from our first fund and early investments in our second,’ said co-founder and senior partner Sumeet Nindrajog. The Mumbai-based investment firm closed its first fund with a corpus of ₹760 crore in 2017, followed by a ₹650 crore Fund II in 2022 during the pandemic. As its previous funds attracted a mix of family offices, institutions and fund of funds from both global as well as domestic investors, its largest fund will target a similar base. With eight investments in each fund, Paragon focuses on financial services, consumer, healthcare and manufacturing. It expects to complete two more deals in six months to wrap up deployment of its second fund. Historically, it has exited investments through a mix of IPOs, strategic sales and secondary sales. Fund I invested in Capacit’e Infraprojects, Maini Precision Products, InCred Finance, Chai Point, InCred Capital, Cravatex Brands, SME Corner and eShakti. The second fund backed Saarathi Finance, Niva Bupa, mCaffeine, GoBolt, Everest and Tendercuts. Nindrajog said the firm’s thesis and evaluation strategy are built on defensible sectors such as financial inclusion, healthcare access and domestic consumption, and it has not seen significant business impact on portfolio companies despite geopolitical or macroeconomic factors. Fund III is likely to make 10-12 investments focused on old-economy businesses.

headline: IPO pipeline strengthens; 38 firms file draft papers in March
text: As many as 38 companies, including Manipal Health Enterprises and SBI Funds Management, filed preliminary IPO papers with Sebi in March 2026, signalling improving issuer sentiment even as regulatory timelines partly drove the surge. This marks a jump from 22 filings in March 2025 and 16 in March 2024, indicating a stronger IPO pipeline. The momentum is expected to continue, with several high-profile companies, including the National Stock Exchange and Reliance Industries’ telecom arm Jio, preparing to submit their draft papers in the coming weeks, according to merchant banking sources. Besides, Sembcorp’s Indian green-energy arm, Sweden-based PlaySimple, TPG-backed online lending platform Fibe and BatterySmart are also likely to file DRHPs soon. Of the 38 firms that filed draft papers, nine companies, including Zetwerk, Rediff.com India, SNVA Traveltech, Torrent Gas, Synergy Advanced Metals, Garuda Aerospace and Sohan Lal Commodity Management, opted for the confidential filing route. According to an Axis Capital report, 64 companies are awaiting Sebi clearance, while 124 firms received regulatory approval but are yet to hit the market. Another 20 companies filed confidential DRHPs since March 2025. The report said FY26 saw 109 mainboard IPOs, of which 69 listed above their issue price, while three firms were yet to debut on the bourses as of 31 March. The IPO market is expected to gain further momentum in Q1 of FY27, supported by a robust pipeline and a large number of companies waiting for Sebi approval or holding valid approvals for launch. So far in 2026, 18 firms launched IPOs, with eight issues hitting the market in March despite volatile conditions. Market participants said the spike reflects a combination of improved issuer confidence and regulatory compliance pushing filings before March-end.

headline: War, rupee hit travel fintechs
text: Travel- and foreign-exchange-focused fintechs such as Niyo, Scapia, BookMyForex and Thomas Cook India are facing a double hit from the war in West Asia and from the persistent weakness in the Indian rupee—both forex usage and remittances have fallen. Most users are opting to carry more cash than cards and prepaid wallets as they become cautious about travel, even to regions outside the Gulf Cooperation Council. They are increasingly opting to withdraw cash in part or in full from forex cards and wallets upon arrival rather than continuing to hold balances. The war has also disrupted business payment flows and cross-border settlements, as local banking operations in the region have been affected. Travel fintech Niyo said travellers are rebalancing usage as currency volatility and regional uncertainty rise. Discretionary travel to GCC destinations has virtually stopped for now, with demand shifting to the Far East and Southeast Asia. The fintech’s product mix has shifted from traditionally card-heavy GCC travel to destinations where cards and cash are used more evenly. ‘Forex cash is picking up significantly, and travellers now prefer to carry two instruments instead of one, so they have a fallback if one stops working or becomes harder to access,’ said Niyo chief executive Amit Talwar. ATM withdrawals in affected countries have risen as users pull out balances and hold physical cash as a safeguard. Scapia said it is seeing a decline in demand for visas, experiences and travel to Dubai and Abu Dhabi, although overall travel demand is holding with leisure travellers shifting to domestic and East and Southeast Asian routes. Rising crude prices and a weaker rupee are raising airfares and insurance costs, said economists, while geopolitical risks have caused rerouting, higher insurance and cancellations. BookMyForex said the disruption includes delays in forex transfers to Indians abroad for university fees and other payments. Thomas Cook India said currency uncertainty is changing traveller behaviour at the point of purchase, with many leisure travellers splitting purchases into tranches and carrying smaller amounts before departure. The hit is not confined to travel and forex. Remittances are suffering too. While remittances to India usually increase when the rupee weakens, this time inflows have been slower amid concerns of job losses and businesses shutting down in the Gulf. Bank and fintech executives said that if this continues, there will definitely be disruption, with the medium-term impact likely to be felt across the system.

headline: Should RIL clarify Trump claim?
text: More than three weeks since US President Donald Trump announced an investment by ‘Reliance’ in a new oil refinery in his country, a lack of clarity from both the Mukesh Ambani-led company and India’s two top stock exchanges on the subject has exposed gaps in India’s rumour verification rules, experts said. Some experts believe Reliance Industries should have provided further clarity on whether it was investing in the US, while others think the situation falls within the grey area of the disclosure rules governing listed companies. However, experts say India’s two top stock exchanges—the BSE and the National Stock Exchange—could have used their discretion to seek clarification from Reliance Industries, as they often do with other firms for matters of far less significance. Rumour verification is governed by Sebi’s listing regulations, amended in 2024 to link verification to stock price movement rather than event materiality. For a stock priced above ₹200, such as Reliance Industries, the price movement threshold is 3% relative to the benchmark. This threshold was not breached on 11 March, the day after Trump’s announcement. On 10 March, Trump announced on social media that America First Refining, a Texas-based firm, was opening the first new oil refinery in the US in over 50 years. He thanked partners in India and ‘their largest privately held Energy Company, Reliance’ for the investment.
